definition_zh: 模具；模子；霉；霉菌；塑造；使成形
definition_en: a hollow container that gives shape to soft material; a soft fungus that grows on damp food or surfaces; to press material into a shape, or to influence how a person develops
core_image: 木框里压满湿泥，倒扣在案板上，一只碗的形状脱了出来
scene: 陶艺课的窗边，师傅把湿泥一点点按进木框，再倒扣在木板上。 She pressed the clay into a wooden mould and left it near the window to dry.
sceneCN: 这里「mould」是「模具、模子」（第 1 个义项：让软材料成形的凹型容器）；句意为她把陶土按进木模具，放在窗边晾干。画面里能想见：木框、湿泥与倒扣出来的碗坯。

collocations.zh: 按照……的模式；带有……的风格

derivatives.zh: 由 mould 加 -ing 构成，义为「模制品；建筑线脚」
由 mould 加 -y 构成，义为「发霉的；有霉味的」
由 mould 加 -able 构成，义为「可塑的；容易成形的」
由 mould 加 -er 构成，义为「制模工；模塑工」

senses.title: A hollow container that gives a shape to soft material
senses.definition: a hollow container with a particular shape, into which soft material is pressed so that it takes that shape
senses.definitionCN: 具有特定形状的空心容器，把软材料压进去，材料就随之成型
senses.example: She pressed the clay into a wooden mould and left it near the window to dry.
senses.exampleCN: 她把陶土按进木模具，放在窗边晾干。
senses.why: The shaping word goes back to Latin modulus, a small measure; a mould is a measured hollow, so its size is settled before any material enters.
senses.whyCN: 表示「成形」的那个词可追到拉丁语 modulus（小尺度）；模子正是一个量好的空腔，材料还没进去，成品的尺寸就已经定死。

senses.title: A soft fungus growing on damp food or surfaces
senses.definition: a green, grey or white growth of fungus that appears on old food, damp walls or leather
senses.definitionCN: 长在陈旧食物、潮湿墙面或皮革上的灰绿、灰白软质真菌
senses.example: There was grey mould along the bathroom tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 浴室瓷砖的缝隙里长着灰霉。
senses.why: This sense is a different word that shares the spelling; it usually grows where things stay damp and begin to break down, and dictionaries keep it apart from the shaping word.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是共用同一拼写的另一个词；它总长在潮湿、开始腐烂的东西上，词典把它与表示成形的那个词分开处理。

senses.title: To press a soft material into a shape
senses.definition: to press clay, dough or another soft substance into a particular shape, by hand or in a container
senses.definitionCN: 用手或容器把陶土、面团等柔软物质压成某个形状
senses.example: He moulded the wet sand into a tiny castle.
senses.exampleCN: 他把湿沙子塑成一座小城堡。
senses.why: If the noun is the measured cavity, the verb is the act of filling it; the word moves from the tool to the work done with the tool.
senses.whyCN: 如果名词是那个量好的空腔，动词就是往里填的动作；词于是从工具转到用工具做的那件事。

senses.title: To shape a person's character or beliefs
senses.definition: to influence strongly how someone's character, habits or beliefs develop over time
senses.definitionCN: 强烈影响某人的性格、习惯或信念在长期中如何发展
senses.example: Years of reading moulded her into a patient observer.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的阅读把她塑造成一个有耐心的观察者。
senses.why: A child is soft material in the hands of family and teachers, so the same verb for pressing clay into a mould is used for forming a mind.
senses.whyCN: 孩子在家和老师手里就是软的材料，于是那个「把泥按进模子」的动词被借来形容心智的形成。

intro.en: Mould has two separate histories: the shaping word runs back to a Latin measure, while the fungus word has its own uncertain origin.
intro.cn: mould 有两段各自独立的来历：表示「成形」的词可追到拉丁语的尺度，表示「霉」的词另有来源，确切来历不确定。

items.en: Modulus meant a small measure, a diminutive of modus, and it named the fixed size against which things were checked.
items.cn: modulus 意为「小尺度」，是 modus 的指小形式，指用来核对事物的既定尺寸。

items.en: Old French modle took the word as a pattern or model, the shape a finished object should follow.
items.cn: 古法语把词写作 modle，指样板或模型，即成品应当照着做的形状。

items.en: Middle English used mold for the hollow pattern that potters and metal workers filled with their material.
items.cn: 中古英语用 mold 指陶工与金属工匠往里填料的空心模范。

items.en: The fungus sense is a separate word of uncertain origin; it is often linked to Scandinavian words for mildew and was influenced by the old earth word.
items.cn: 表示霉的义项是另一个来源不确定的词，一般认为与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示霉的词有关，并受到表示泥土的古词影响。

items.en: Modern English keeps British mould and American mold, and adds the verb senses of shaping material and shaping a mind.
items.cn: 现代英语保留英式 mould 与美式 mold 两种拼写，并发展出塑造材料与塑造心智的动词义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the British and American spellings and the shaping family; the near-meaning group gathers words for casting, forming and fungus.
note.cn: 形近组收英式与美式拼写以及「成形」词族；近义组收表示浇铸、成形与真菌的词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of mould, used for the container, the fungus and the verb.
entries.definitionCN: mould 的美式拼写，容器、霉与动词都用它。

entries.definition: Something made in a mould, or a shaped strip along a wall.
entries.definitionCN: 在模子里做出来的东西，或墙面上成形的线脚。

entries.definition: Covered with mould or smelling of damp.
Soft enough to be pressed into a shape.
A small measure in Latin, the source of mould and of module.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中的「小尺度」，是 mould 与 module 的来源。

entries.definition: To pour melted metal or another liquid material into a mould.
entries.definitionCN: 把熔化的金属等液体材料浇进模子。

entries.definition: To give something a particular form.
entries.definitionCN: 给某物一个特定的形状。

entries.definition: To make or develop into a particular shape or arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 使成为或发展成某种形状、结构。

entries.definition: A plant-like growth such as mould, mildew or mushroom.
entries.definitionCN: 霉、白粉病或蘑菇一类近似植物的生长物。

normalIntro.en: One spelling carries a family about measured cavities and a separate word about damp growth; keeping the two apart makes the senses easier to hold.
normalIntro.cn: 同一个拼写承载着「量好的空腔」这一词族，也承载着另一个表示潮湿生长的词；把两者分开，义项就好记了。

normal.en: Modulus is Latin for a small measure, so a mould is a cavity whose size was decided in advance.
normal.cn: modulus 是拉丁语的「小尺度」，所以模子就是尺寸事先定好的空腔。

normal.en: Moulding adds -ing: the object that comes out of the mould, or the shaped strip on a wall.
normal.cn: moulding 加 -ing：从模子里出来的物件，或墙上成形的线脚。

normal.en: Mouldy adds -y: full of mould, therefore spoiled and damp.
normal.cn: mouldy 加 -y：长满霉，因此坏了、带着潮气。

normal.en: Mouldable adds -able: able to take a shape, like wet clay.
normal.cn: mouldable 加 -able：能够被塑成形状，就像湿陶土。

normal.en: British mould and American mold differ only in the u, just as colour and color do.
normal.cn: 英式与美式的差别只在那个 u，就像 colour 与 color 一样。

abstract.en: A mould is a promise made before the material arrives: the result is already written in the cavity.
abstract.cn: 模子是材料到来之前就许下的承诺：结果早已写在空腔里。

abstract.en: Shaping clay and shaping a child use one verb because both need gentle, repeated pressure.
abstract.cn: 塑造陶土与塑造孩子共用一个动词，因为两者都需要温和而反复的按压。

abstract.en: The fungus sense reminds us that damp, soft places quietly rewrite whatever rests in them.
abstract.cn: 表示霉的义项提醒人：潮湿柔软的地方会悄悄改写停放在那里的东西。

examples.en: She pressed the clay into a wooden mould and left it near the window to dry.
examples.cn: 她把陶土按进木模具，放在窗边晾干。

examples.en: There was grey mould along the bathroom tiles.
examples.cn: 浴室瓷砖的缝隙里长着灰霉。

examples.en: Years of reading moulded her into a patient observer.
examples.cn: 多年的阅读把她塑造成一个有耐心的观察者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「模得」——把湿泥按进框里，一脱模就得到一个形状；mould 既是模具，也是塑形。

root: 表示「成形」的 mould 来自拉丁语 modulus（小尺度，modus 的指小形式），经古法语 modle 进入英语；表示「霉」的义项一般认为另有来源，确切词源不确定；英式写 mould，美式写 mold。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a measured hollow that decides a shape; from it come the container, the pressing action and the shaping of a mind, while the fungus sense is a separate old word sharing the spelling.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个决定形状的量好空腔；由此分出容器、按压动作与心智的塑造，而表示霉的义项是共用拼写的另一个古词。

intro.en: A Latin measure word, its diminutive, a French pattern word and English endings from -ing to -able hold the shaping family together; the fungus sense sits outside it.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语尺度词、它的指小形式、一个法语「样板」词，加上从 -ing 到 -able 的英语词尾，撑起了「成形」这一族；表示霉的义项在这一族之外。

latinIntro.en: Modus and its diminutive modulus belong to the Latin vocabulary of measuring; the fungus sense has no reliable Latin cognate and is left out of this list.
latinIntro.cn: modus 及其指小形式 modulus 属于拉丁语「量度」词汇；表示霉的义项没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此不列入。

definition_zh: （鸟兽的）爪；（蟹虾的）钳；用爪抓
definition_en: a sharp curved nail on the foot of a bird or animal, the pincer of a crab, or to scratch with such a nail
core_image: 一只弯钩般的利爪扣住树枝
scene: 猫伏在窗台上，尾巴慢慢摆。 The cat dug one claw into the cushion and yawned.
sceneCN: 这里 claw 指「爪」（第 1 个义项：鸟兽脚上弯曲的尖甲）；句意是猫把一只爪子抠进坐垫，打了个哈欠。

senses.title: A sharp curved nail
senses.definition: a hard curved nail on the foot of a bird or animal
senses.definitionCN: 鸟或兽脚上坚硬而弯曲的指甲
senses.example: The owl's claws closed around the branch.
senses.exampleCN: 猫头鹰的爪子扣住了树枝。
senses.why: The old English word named the hooked nail itself, before it named any action.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语词先指弯钩状的甲本身，后来才指动作。

senses.title: A crab's pincer
senses.definition: one of the two pinching limbs of a crab, lobster or scorpion
senses.definitionCN: 蟹、龙虾或蝎子两只可夹合的肢体之一
senses.example: The crab raised one claw above the sand.
senses.exampleCN: 螃蟹在沙上举起一只钳。
senses.why: A pincer is a hooked gripper, so the same word covers the limb of a shellfish.
senses.whyCN: 钳是钩状的抓握器，于是同一个词也覆盖甲壳类的肢体。

senses.title: To scratch with claws
senses.definition: to tear or pull at something with claws or fingers
senses.definitionCN: 用爪或手指撕扯、抓挠某物
senses.example: The dog clawed at the door to get out.
senses.exampleCN: 狗抓着门想出去。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb once people described what the claw does.
senses.whyCN: 当人们开始描述爪子所做的事，名词就转为动词。

intro.en: Claw is an old English word for a hooked nail, unchanged in meaning for a thousand years.
intro.cn: claw 是古英语里表示钩状甲的词，千年来含义几乎未变。

items.en: Clawu named the nail of a bird or beast.
items.cn: clawu 指鸟兽的指甲。

items.en: The form became claw and also named a pincer.
items.cn: 词形变为 claw，也用来指钳。

items.en: The verb appeared, meaning to tear with claws.
items.cn: 动词形式出现，意为用爪撕抓。

items.en: The word entered figures of speech about struggling upward.
items.cn: 这个词进入表示奋力向上攀爬的比喻。

items.en: Claw covers nails, pincers and the act of scratching.
items.cn: claw 兼指爪、钳与抓挠的动作。

normal.en: Birds scratch with a claw, crabs pinch with a claw, and both are hooks.

normal.en: The plural claws serves both the noun and the verb.

branches.en: The hooked nail belongs to birds and beasts.

branches.cn: 爪与抓是工具及其使用。

branches.en: Both are hard curved grippers.
branches.cn: 两者都是坚硬弯曲的抓握器。

intro.en: The noun takes a plural and a verb ending, and grows two adjectives and a prefixed verb.
intro.cn: 这个名词接复数与动词词尾，并长出两个形容词和一个前缀动词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base: claw is a native Germanic word.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语词基：claw 是日耳曼语本族词。

items.meaning: a hooked nail or to scratch
items.example: The bird has one damaged claw.
items.exampleCN: 这只鸟有一只爪受了伤。

items.example: Its claws are longer than its beak.
It was clawing at the wire.
A clawed foot gripped the ledge.
items.exampleCN: 一只带爪的脚扣住窗台。
这只无爪的鸟无法捕猎。

items.example: Vets rarely declaw a cat now.
items.exampleCN: 如今兽医很少给猫去爪。

items.meaning: a hammer with a split hook
items.example: He pulled the nail with a claw hammer.
items.exampleCN: 他用羊角锤拔出了钉子。

definition_zh: 夸大；夸张；使过大
definition_en: to describe something as bigger or better than it is
core_image: 一个小水坑被画成一片汪洋
scene: 他总爱夸大自己的经历，把一次小旅行说成冒险。 He always tends to exaggerate his experiences, turning a short trip into an adventure.
sceneCN: 这里 exaggerate 是「夸大」（第 1 个义项：把事情说得比实际更大）；句意：他总爱夸大自己的经历，把一次小旅行说成冒险。

senses.title: Making too much
senses.definition: to make something seem larger or better
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物显得更大或更好
senses.example: She exaggerated the size of the fish.
senses.exampleCN: 她夸大了那条鱼的大小。
senses.why: Ex- out and aggerare to pile up give the image of piling on.
senses.whyCN: ex-（出）与 aggerare（堆积）构成往上堆的意象。

senses.title: Overstating a feeling
senses.definition: to say something is stronger than it is
senses.definitionCN: 把某种感受说得过强
senses.example: He exaggerated his pain to get sympathy.
senses.exampleCN: 他为了博取同情夸大了疼痛。
senses.why: The same piling up applies to feelings.
senses.whyCN: 同样的堆积也适用于感受。

senses.title: To make too large
senses.definition: to make something larger than normal
senses.definitionCN: 使某物大于正常
senses.example: The wide lens exaggerates the distance.
senses.exampleCN: 广角镜头会夸大距离感。
senses.why: The visual sense keeps the literal idea of enlargement.
senses.whyCN: 视觉含义保留了放大的字面意思。

intro.en: Exaggerate comes from Latin exaggerare, to heap up.
intro.cn: exaggerate 源自拉丁语 exaggerare（堆高）。

items.en: Agger means a heap.
items.cn: agger 意为堆。

items.en: Aggerare means to heap up.
items.cn: aggerare 意为堆起。

items.en: Exaggerare means to pile up.
items.cn: exaggerare 意为堆积。

items.en: Exaggerate first means to heap up.
items.cn: exaggerate 最初意为堆高。

items.en: It means to overstate.
items.cn: 它逐渐指夸大其词。

note.en: Exaggerate is to describe too strongly; overstate is its formal twin.
note.cn: exaggerate 指描述得过头；overstate 是它更正式的同义词。

entries.definition: a statement that overstates
made to seem larger
a person who exaggerates
to state something too strongly
to make a number or claim seem larger
to make something appear larger

normalIntro.en: Exaggerate is piling extra words on a small fact.
normalIntro.cn: exaggerate 是在小事实上一层层堆词。

normal.en: Exaggerate the danger means make it seem worse.
normal.cn: exaggerate the danger 意为把危险说得更严重。

normal.en: Exaggerate the size means claim it is bigger.
normal.cn: exaggerate the size 意为声称尺寸更大。

normal.en: Grossly exaggerate means overstate very much.
normal.cn: grossly exaggerate 意为严重夸大。

normal.en: Without exaggerating means speaking plainly.
normal.cn: without exaggerating 意为毫不夸张地说。

normal.en: Compare overstate: exaggerate is everyday, overstate is formal.
normal.cn: 对比 overstate：exaggerate 更日常，overstate 更正式。

abstract.en: Picture a small puddle drawn as a wide sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小水坑被画成一片汪洋。

abstract.en: Imagine a shadow at sunset stretching far beyond its owner.
abstract.cn: 想象日落时影子被拉得远远超过本人。

abstract.en: Think of a story that grows with every telling.
abstract.cn: 想象一个每讲一次就变大的故事。

examples.en: Don't exaggerate the difficulties.
examples.cn: 不要夸大困难。

examples.en: The report exaggerates the benefits of the plan.
examples.cn: 报告夸大了计划的好处。

examples.en: He tends to exaggerate when he is nervous.
examples.cn: 他紧张时容易夸大其词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ agger（堆）」——往事实外面不断堆东西，就是夸大。

root: 拉丁语 exaggerare（堆高）＝ ex-（出）＋ aggerare（堆积）→ exaggerate，核心义「越堆越高、言过其实」。

sensesIntro.en: Exaggerate means to make a fact seem larger, to overstate a feeling, and even to enlarge an image.
sensesIntro.cn: exaggerate 指把事实说得更大、把感受说过头，也可指放大图像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small puddle drawn as a wide sea.
core.cn: 核心意象：小水坑被画成汪洋。

branches.en: Piling onto a fact is the core.
branches.cn: 在事实上一层层堆积是核心。

branches.en: Feelings can be overdone too.
branches.cn: 感受也能被夸大。

branches.en: Images can be enlarged as well.
branches.cn: 图像也能被放大。

branches.en: Facts and feelings both grow in the telling.
branches.cn: 事实与感受都在讲述中变大。

branches.en: Words and lenses both enlarge.
branches.cn: 言语与镜头都在放大。

intro.en: Exaggerate joins ex-, out, to the Latin root agger, a heap.
intro.cn: exaggerate 由 ex-（出）与拉丁词根 agger（堆）组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin exaggerare is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exaggerare 是直接来源。

definition_zh: 拒绝；拒绝给予
definition_en: the act of saying no to an offer or a request; the act of not granting something
core_image: 合同被推回桌对面，一只手轻轻摇了摇头
scene: 招聘方把合同推回桌对面，摇了摇头，没有多说什么。 Her refusal to sign the contract surprised everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 refusal 是「拒绝」（第 1 个义项：表示不接受、不答应）；句意为她拒签合同，让所有人都很意外。画面里可留意：被推回的合同、轻轻摇头的手。

senses.title: The act of saying no
senses.definition: the act of declining an offer, an invitation, or an order
senses.definitionCN: 不接受提议、邀请或命令的行为
senses.example: Her refusal to sign the contract surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 她拒签合同，让所有人都很意外。
senses.why: The noun names the no itself, and the Latin verb behind it images a pouring back: the offer is returned to the one who made it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名的是「不」本身，而其背后的拉丁动词描绘「倒回去」：提议被退回给提出的人。

senses.title: The act of not granting
senses.definition: the act of withholding something that was asked for
senses.definitionCN: 不给予别人所求之物的行为
senses.example: The refusal of a visa left the whole family in limbo.
senses.exampleCN: 签证被拒，让整个家庭悬而未决。
senses.why: When what is turned back is a gift or a permission rather than an offer, the same noun means a withholding.
senses.whyCN: 当被退回的是赠予或许可而不是提议时，同一个名词就表示「不给」。

intro.en: Refusal is the noun of refuse, and its oldest image is a pouring back: what was offered is sent back to its source.
intro.cn: refusal 是 refuse 的名词，其最古老的意象是「倒回去」：被提供的东西被送回原处。

items.en: Fundere meant to pour, and its participle supplied the image of something poured out.
items.cn: fundere 意为倾倒，其分词提供了「被倒出之物」的意象。

items.en: Refusare probably joined re-, back, with the participle of fundere, giving the sense of pouring back and so rejecting.
items.cn: refusare 很可能由 re-（往回）与 fundere 的分词构成，意为倒回去，因而表示拒绝。

items.en: Old French refuser meant to refuse or reject, and English took the verb from it.
items.cn: 古法语 refuser 意为拒绝或驳回，英语由此借入动词。

items.en: English added the noun ending -al and made refusal, the act of the verb.
items.cn: 英语加上名词词尾 -al 造出 refusal，表示该动词的行为。

items.en: In modern use a refusal can be polite or blunt, and the word often carries the weight of a broken expectation.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，拒绝可以是客气的，也可以是生硬的，这个词常带着期待落空的分量。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that begin like refuse; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for saying no.
note.cn: 形近组收与 refuse 开头相近的词；近义组收表示「说不」的名词。

entries.definition: To say no to something.
To prove something wrong.
To fill again with fuel.
A statement that something is not true or not granted.
The act of refusing to accept.
A polite refusal.
An official power to reject.

normalIntro.en: The noun is a no made into a thing: an offer comes to the table and is pushed back.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是把「不」变成一件东西：提议来到桌前，又被推了回去。

normal.en: Refuse is the act, refusal is the no itself.
normal.cn: refuse 是动作，refusal 是那个「不」本身。

normal.en: A blunt refusal leaves no room for argument.
normal.cn: a blunt refusal 不留争辩的余地。

normal.en: Refusal to comply with the order brought a fine.
normal.cn: 拒绝服从命令招来了罚款。

normal.en: The refusal of a visa is a no written on paper.
normal.cn: 签证被拒，是写在纸上的一声「不」。

normal.en: Refusal ends in al, the ending that turns verbs into acts.
normal.cn: refusal 以 al 结尾，这个词尾把动词变成行为。

abstract.en: A refusal can protect a person as often as it disappoints one.
abstract.cn: 拒绝既能保护一个人，也常让人失望。

abstract.en: The right to refuse is the smallest unit of freedom.
abstract.cn: 拒绝的权利，是自由最小的单位。

abstract.en: A clear refusal is kinder than a slow maybe.
abstract.cn: 明确的拒绝，比拖延的「也许」更善意。

examples.en: Her refusal to sign the contract surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 她拒签合同，让所有人都很意外。

examples.en: The refusal of a visa left the whole family in limbo.
examples.cn: 签证被拒，让整个家庭悬而未决。

examples.en: He met every question with a polite refusal to answer.
examples.cn: 他对每个问题都以礼貌的拒绝作答。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回）加 fus（倒）加 al（名词尾）：把递过来的东西倒推回去，就是拒绝；把它变成一件事，就是 refusal。

root: 拉丁 fundere（倾倒）→ refusare（倒回、拒绝）→ 古法语 refuser → 英语 refuse；加 -al 构成 refusal。同族有 refuse、refusable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a returned offer; the senses move from declining what is offered to withholding what is asked.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被退回的提议」；义项从拒绝所提供之物，到不给予所请求之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a contract pushed back across a table with a shake of the head.
core.cn: 核心意象：合同被推回桌对面，一只手轻轻摇了摇头。

branches.en: a signed page left unsigned
branches.cn: 一页没有被签下的合同

branches.en: a visa stamped no
branches.cn: 盖了「不」的签证

branches.en: an offer returned and a request denied
branches.cn: 提议被退回，请求被驳回

branches.en: a polite sentence with no room to argue
branches.cn: 一句客气却无可争辩的话

branches.en: a door that stays shut
branches.cn: 一扇一直关着的门

intro.en: A Latin verb of pouring takes a prefix of return, and a noun ending turns the act of pushing an offer back into a thing with a name.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「倾倒」动词接上表返回的前缀，名词词尾再把「把提议推回去」这个动作变成有名字的事物。

latinIntro.en: The base is fundere, to pour; re- means back, and -al forms the noun of action.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 fundere（倾倒）；re- 表「往回」，-al 构成表行为的名词。

definition_zh: 道德上；从道德角度；有道德地；几乎确定地
definition_en: in terms of right and wrong, in a good and honest way, and in the fixed phrase morally certain, almost certainly
core_image: 把同一把尺子举到每个举动前面
scene: 会议室里有人把方案推回桌上，理由只有一句。 She refused, on the grounds that the plan was morally wrong.
sceneCN: 这里是「道德上、从道德角度看」（第 1 个义项：按是非标准评判）；句意为她以这个计划在道德上站不住脚为由拒绝。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、方案纸、推回的手。

pos.zh: 道德上；从道德角度；有道德地

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词词尾 -ly 得到形容词 moral，义为「道德的」
由否定前缀 im- 加 moral 构成，义为「不道德的」
由 moral 加 -istic 构成，义为「说教的；道德主义的」

senses.title: Judged by a moral standard
senses.definition: in terms of right and wrong rather than of profit, taste or law
senses.definitionCN: 按是非来评判，而不是按利益、品味或法律
senses.example: The decision was morally defensible even if it was costly.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定虽然在代价上不小，在道德上却站得住脚。
senses.why: -ly turns the adjective moral into a word for the standpoint from which something is judged.
senses.whyCN: -ly 把形容词 moral 变成表示「从哪个立足点评判」的词。

senses.title: In a good and honest way
senses.definition: in a way that follows accepted standards of good behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 以符合公认良好行为标准的方式
senses.example: They behaved morally when no one was watching.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人看着的时候，他们的行为依然正派。
senses.why: The same adverb can describe the manner of an act, not only the standard used, so it also means acting well.
senses.whyCN: 同一个副词既可以指所用的标准，也可以描述行为的方式，因此也能表示做得正派。

senses.title: Almost certain, in a fixed phrase
senses.definition: used in morally certain or morally sure to mean that something is almost certain to happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于 morally certain 或 morally sure，表示某事几乎肯定会发生
senses.example: It is morally certain that the vote will pass.
senses.exampleCN: 这次表决几乎肯定能通过。
senses.why: The phrase comes from legal and philosophical argument, where a conclusion could be certain for all practical purposes.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法来自法律与哲学的论辩，其中结论可以在一切实际意义上被视为确定。

intro.en: The adverb is a late, regular addition to moral, made with an Old English ending that had already been turning adjectives into adverbs for centuries.
intro.cn: 这个副词是后来在 moral 上按常规加缀构成的，所用的古英语词尾早已把形容词变成副词好几百年了。

items.en: The Latin adjective moralis described whatever concerned character and conduct, and it is the root of the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 moralis 描述一切与品性和行为有关的东西，是这一整族词的根。

items.en: Old French passed the adjective moral to English, still judging behaviour as good or bad.
items.cn: 古法语把形容词 moral 传给英语，仍用来评判行为的好坏。

items.en: Middle English used moral for conduct and, as a noun, for the lesson of a story.
items.cn: 中古英语用 moral 指品行，也作名词指故事的教训。

items.en: The ending -ly descends from Old English -līce, which had long been the standard way to make an adverb from an adjective.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 源自古英语 -līce，早已是把形容词变成副词的标准方式。

items.en: Modern English morally adds that ending to moral and also carries the fixed phrase morally certain.
items.cn: 现代英语的 morally 把这一词尾加在 moral 上，并保留固定说法 morally certain。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms on the same moral stem, while the near-meaning group collects other adverbs of judgement.
note.cn: 形近组收同一道德词干上的形式，近义组收其他表示评判的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective from which this adverb is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 构成这个副词的原形容词。

entries.definition: In a way that goes against moral standards.
Too concerned with judging other people's morals.
entries.definitionCN: 过分热衷于评判他人道德的。

entries.definition: In terms of accepted principles of conduct.
entries.definitionCN: 按公认的行为准则来看。

entries.definition: In a way that shows high moral standards.
entries.definitionCN: 以体现高尚道德的方式。

entries.definition: In a proper and respectable way.

normalIntro.en: The word is an adverb of standard: it does not say what happened, only by which measure it should be weighed.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个关于标准的副词：它不说什么发生了，只说该用哪把尺子去称。

normal.en: morally is moral plus -ly, the adverb ending that descends from Old English -līce.
normal.cn: morally 是 moral 加 -ly，这个副词词尾源自古英语 -līce。

normal.en: The ending turns an adjective of judgement into a word for the manner of judging.
normal.cn: 这个词尾把表示评判的形容词变成表示评判方式的词。

normal.en: In morally wrong the adverb marks the standard being used, not the degree of wrongness.
normal.cn: 在 morally wrong 里，这个副词标出所用的是哪套标准，而不是错误的程度。

normal.en: The fixed phrase morally certain means almost certain, a sense that grew out of legal argument.
normal.cn: 固定说法 morally certain 意为几乎确定，这个含义从法律论辩中长出来。

normal.en: Immoral and morally share a stem: one judges the act, the other judges the manner.
normal.cn: immoral 与 morally 共用词干：一个评判行为，一个评判方式。

abstract.en: An adverb is a lens: morally tells you which lens is being held up.
abstract.cn: 副词像一片镜片：morally 告诉你举起的是哪一片。

abstract.en: The word asks not what happened but by which measure it is weighed.
abstract.cn: 这个词不问发生了什么，只问用哪把尺子去称。

abstract.en: A scale carried outside the body can become a habit carried inside.
abstract.cn: 身外的一杆秤，可以变成随身的一套习惯。

examples.en: The decision was morally defensible even if it was costly.
examples.cn: 这个决定虽然在代价上不小，在道德上却站得住脚。

examples.en: They behaved morally when no one was watching.
examples.cn: 没有人看着的时候，他们的行为依然正派。

examples.en: It is morally certain that the vote will pass.
examples.cn: 这次表决几乎肯定能通过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫惹理」——莫惹道理，凡事从道德上讲；morally 是道德上。

root: 由 moral 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；-ly 源自古英语 -līce，长期用来把形容词变成副词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is judging by a moral standard, and the two further senses cover acting well and the fixed use that means almost certain.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是按道德标准评判；另外两个义项分别覆盖做得正派，以及表示几乎确定的那种固定用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ruler lifted in front of every act, always the same ruler.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一把尺子举在每一个举动前面，永远是同一把。

branches.en: a plan weighed against a rule
branches.cn: 一份方案被放到规则前称量

branches.en: a good deed done with no audience
branches.cn: 无人观看时做的一件好事

branches.en: a forecast that cannot realistically fail
branches.cn: 一个实际上不可能落空的预测

branches.en: a choice both defensible and clean
branches.cn: 一个既站得住脚又干净的选择

branches.en: a manner held to be beyond doubt
branches.cn: 被认为无可置疑的做法

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of conduct plus an Old English adverb ending, with a negative prefix close at hand.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示品行的拉丁形容词加古英语副词词尾，旁边还站着一个否定前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin adjective moralis and its noun moralitas sit directly behind the English adjective and this adverb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 moralis 及其名词 moralitas 直接位于英语形容词与这个副词的背后。

items.meaningCN: 把形容词变成副词的后缀

definition_zh: 摄影师；拍照的人
definition_en: a person who takes photographs, especially as a job or as an art
core_image: 一个人半蹲在路边，相机贴在眼前，等那只鸟起飞
scene: 婚礼现场人来人往，一个背着两台相机的人在人群里挪动脚步，寻找角度。 The photographer waved the family into the last patch of sunlight.
sceneCN: 这里是「摄影师」（第 1 个义项：以拍照为职业的人）；句意为摄影师招手让一家人站到最后那一小块阳光里。背着的相机和寻找角度的动作都指向这个职业身份。

derivatives.zh: photographer 去掉 -er 换 -y，义为「摄影术」；-grapher 指人，-graphy 指技艺
photo- 加 -genic（产生），义为「上相的」

senses.title: A person who takes pictures for a living
senses.definition: a person who takes photographs, especially someone who does it as a job
senses.definitionCN: 拍摄照片的人，尤指以此为职业者
senses.example: The photographer waved the family into the last patch of sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师招手让一家人站到最后一小块阳光里。
senses.why: -er selects the human agent out of the whole act of photographing, so the word names a role rather than a single click of the shutter.
senses.whyCN: -er 从整个拍摄行为里挑出「施动的人」，所以这个词指的是一个角色，而不是某一次按下快门。

senses.title: The person credited for one particular picture
senses.definition: the person who took a particular picture, often named in a credit line
senses.definitionCN: 拍下某张特定照片的人，常在署名中注明
senses.example: The credit line lists her as the photographer of the cover image.
senses.exampleCN: 版权署名把她列为封面照片的拍摄者。
senses.why: The same role word can be pinned to one image: a credit line turns a profession into a signature, which is why the definite article often appears.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示角色的词也能固定到某一幅影像上：署名把职业变成签名，所以这里常带定冠词。

intro.en: Photographer was coined alongside photograph in 1839, once -er was added to the new word for a light-made image.
intro.cn: photographer 与 photograph 同在 1839 年前后被造出，做法是在这个表示感光影像的新词后加 -er。

items.en: Phos, genitive photos, meant light and gave the first element of the new compound.
items.cn: phos 的属格是 photos，意为光，提供了这个新复合词的第一部分。

items.en: Graphein meant to draw or write, and the Greek combining form -graphos already named one who writes or draws.
items.cn: graphein 意为画、写，希腊语的组合成分 -graphos 本来就指书写或描画的人。

items.en: Sir John Herschel is usually credited with photograph, photography and photographer in the same year, when the new process needed names for the image, the craft and the worker.
items.cn: 一般认为 photograph、photography、photographer 都由约翰·赫歇尔在同一年确定；当时这项新工艺正需要给影像、技艺和操作者分别命名。

items.en: English -er marked the doer, so photographer named the person while -graph stayed on the object and -y went to the practice.
items.cn: 英语的 -er 标记施动者，于是 photographer 指人，-graph 留在物件上，-y 则归到技艺。

items.en: The word now covers staff photographers, freelancers and hobbyists, and compounds such as photojournalist build on it.
items.cn: 现代英语里它既指机构摄影师，也指自由职业者和爱好者，photojournalist 这类复合词也建在它上面。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the same Greek family, with the ending showing which member is meant; the near-meaning group collects other camera workers and image makers.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊词族的成员，靠结尾区分所指；近义组收其他与相机、影像打交道的人。

entries.definition: The image itself, ending in -graph rather than in -er.
entries.definitionCN: 影像本身，结尾是 -graph 而不是 -er。

entries.definition: The art or trade, ending in -graphy instead of naming a person.
entries.definitionCN: 摄影的技艺或行业，结尾是 -graphy，不指人。

entries.definition: The adjective for anything relating to the making of photographs.
entries.definitionCN: 表示与拍摄照片有关的形容词。

entries.definition: A photographer who reports news through pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 用照片报道新闻的摄影师。

entries.definition: A person who operates a camera, especially for film or television.
entries.definitionCN: 操作摄影机的人，尤指影视拍摄。

entries.definition: The person responsible for the camera and lighting of a film.
entries.definitionCN: 负责一部电影摄影与布光的人。

entries.definition: A person who makes art, including someone whose photographs are shown as art.
entries.definitionCN: 从事艺术创作的人，包括把照片作为艺术展出的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is a job title built by suffix, and its neighbours show exactly which suffix does which job.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是靠后缀搭出来的职业名称，它的同族词正好显示每个后缀各管什么。

normal.en: Photographer is photograph plus -er, and -er points at the person who performs the action.
normal.cn: photographer 就是 photograph 加 -er，而 -er 指向执行动作的人。

normal.en: The family divides neatly: -graph the picture, -grapher the person, -graphy the practice.
normal.cn: 这一族分得很清楚：-graph 是照片，-grapher 是人，-graphy 是技艺。

normal.en: Greek -graphos already meant one who writes or draws, so -grapher repeats an old idea in English spelling.
normal.cn: 希腊语 -graphos 本来就指书写或描画的人，所以 -grapher 只是用英语拼写重复了一个旧概念。

normal.en: A press photographer works to a deadline; a wedding photographer works to a family's memory, but both carry the same -er.
normal.cn: 新闻摄影师赶截稿时间，婚礼摄影师对着一家人的记忆工作，但两者都带同一个 -er。

normal.en: A photo credit is simply the place where this -er word is printed under the image.
normal.cn: 照片署名无非是把带 -er 的这个词印在影像下方。

abstract.en: The photographer stands between the world and the picture, deciding what the rest of us will see.
abstract.cn: 摄影师站在世界与照片之间，替其余的人决定可以看到什么。

abstract.en: The person who spends a life behind a lens is often the one missing from the family album.
abstract.cn: 常年站在镜头后的人，往往正是家庭相册里缺席的那一个。

abstract.en: The suffix is small but decisive: without -er there is only an image, with it there is a witness.
abstract.cn: 这个后缀很小却很关键：没有 -er 只有一张影像，有了它就有了一个见证者。

examples.en: The photographer waved the family into the last patch of sunlight.
examples.cn: 摄影师招手让一家人站到最后一小块阳光里。

examples.en: She hired a photographer for the opening night.
examples.cn: 她为开幕之夜请了一位摄影师。

examples.en: Press photographers waited outside the court all morning.
examples.cn: 新闻摄影师在法院外等了一上午。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「否头格拉弗」——把光写下来的人；记住 photographer 是摄影师，结尾 -er 专指人。

root: 希腊语 phos/photos（光）+ graphein（写、画）+ 英语 -er（人）；同一词干上 -graph 是成品，-grapher 是人，-graphy 是技艺。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the person who operates the camera; the two senses split between the job and the name attached to one particular picture.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是操作相机的人；两个义项分别指这份职业，以及某一幅具体照片的署名者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure kneeling on the pavement, one eye behind the camera, waiting for the exact second.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人跪在人行道上，一只眼睛贴在相机后，等那个准确的瞬间。

branches.en: a wedding photographer stepping between the tables
branches.cn: 在餐桌间穿行的婚礼摄影师

branches.en: a press photographer waiting behind the police line
branches.cn: 警戒线后等待的新闻摄影师

branches.en: a name printed in small type under a cover image
branches.cn: 封面图下小字印着的名字

branches.en: the same name as a job and as an author
branches.cn: 同一个名字既是职业也是作者

branches.en: a low angle taken from one knee
branches.cn: 单膝跪地拍出的低角度

intro.en: The word is the meeting point of three formatives, and the last one decides that a person, not a picture or a craft, is meant.
intro.cn: 这个词是三个构词成分的交汇处，最后一个成分决定了它指人，而不是指照片或技艺。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的词根是希腊语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: turns the person-word into the practice-word
items.meaningCN: 把指人的词变成指技艺的词

definition_zh: 真诚的；诚恳的；由衷的
definition_en: honest and meaning what one says
core_image: 一个人直视你的眼睛，说话时没有躲闪
scene: 他的道歉听起来很真诚。 His apology sounded sincere.
sceneCN: 这里 sincere 是「真诚的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的道歉听起来很真诚。

senses.title: Honest in feeling
senses.definition: honest and not pretending
senses.definitionCN: 诚实而不做假的
senses.example: His apology sounded sincere.
senses.exampleCN: 他的道歉听起来很真诚。
senses.why: This is the central sense of a true heart.
senses.whyCN: 这是「真心」的核心义项。

senses.title: Truly felt
senses.definition: felt deeply and meant fully
senses.definitionCN: 感受深切并完全出于本意的
senses.example: Please accept my sincere thanks.
senses.exampleCN: 请接受我衷心的感谢。
senses.why: The same honesty applied to thanks and belief.
senses.whyCN: 同样的诚实也用于感谢与信念。

intro.en: Sincere came to English from Latin through French.
intro.cn: sincere 经法语从拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Sincerus meant clean, pure, or whole.
items.cn: sincerus 意为洁净、纯粹或完整。

items.en: Sincere kept the idea of being pure.
items.cn: sincere 保留了「纯粹」的含义。

items.en: English borrowed it for honest feelings.
items.cn: 英语借入它来表示诚实的情感。

items.en: It described a person without pretense.
items.cn: 它形容不装假的人。

items.en: It is fixed in letters as a closing word.
items.cn: 它固定用于书信结尾。

note.en: Sincere is compared with similar-looking words and words for honesty.
note.cn: 把 sincere 与形近词以及表示诚实的词作比较。

entries.definition: honesty of feeling
with beautiful views
calm and peaceful
truthful
real and true
serious and sincere

normalIntro.en: Sincere means the inside matches the words.
normalIntro.cn: sincere 意味着内心与言语一致。

normal.en: His apology sounded sincere.
normal.cn: 他的道歉听起来很真诚。

normal.en: Please accept my sincere thanks.
normal.cn: 请接受我衷心的感谢。

normal.en: She gave me a sincere smile.
normal.cn: 她给了我一个真诚的微笑。

normal.en: He made a sincere effort to change.
normal.cn: 他真心实意地努力改变。

normal.en: Their belief in the plan was sincere.
normal.cn: 他们对这个计划的信念是真诚的。

abstract.en: Sincerity is a window with clean glass.
abstract.cn: 真诚是一扇玻璃洁净的窗。

abstract.en: A sincere word needs no loud voice.
abstract.cn: 真诚的话不需要大声。

abstract.en: What is pure inside shows outside.
abstract.cn: 内心纯粹，外表自现。

examples.en: His apology sounded sincere.
examples.cn: 他的道歉听起来很真诚。

examples.en: She gave me a sincere smile.
examples.cn: 她给了我一个真诚的微笑。

examples.en: Please accept my sincere thanks.
examples.cn: 请接受我衷心的感谢。

dict_mnemonic.text: sincere 加 -ly 成 sincerely（真诚地），加 -ity 成 sincerity（真诚）；写信结尾 Yours sincerely 就是「您真诚的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 sincerus（洁净的、纯粹的），核心义「内心纯净不装假」。

sensesIntro.en: Sincere means honest in feeling or truly felt.
sensesIntro.cn: sincere 意为真诚的或由衷的。

core.en: A heart that matches the words.
core.cn: 与言语一致的内心。

branches.en: An apology carries no hidden plan.
branches.cn: 道歉里没有藏着别的打算。

branches.en: Thanks rise from real feeling.
branches.cn: 感谢出自真实的感受。

branches.en: Honest words and deep feeling belong together.
branches.cn: 诚实的话与深切的情感相伴。

branches.en: A smile shows what the face does not hide.
branches.cn: 微笑露出脸上未加掩饰的东西。

branches.en: A belief held without pretense stands firm.
branches.cn: 不带伪装的信念更加坚定。

intro.en: Sincere builds words for honest feeling.
intro.cn: sincere 构成表示真诚情感的词。

latinIntro.en: Sincere goes back to Latin sincerus.
latinIntro.cn: sincere 可追溯至拉丁语 sincerus。

items.example: My sincerest wishes go with you.
items.exampleCN: 我最真诚的祝福与你同在。

items.example: He gave sincere thanks to the doctor.
items.exampleCN: 他向医生表达了衷心的感谢。

items.example: It was a sincere belief, not a slogan.
items.exampleCN: 那是真诚的信念，不是口号。
他的赞美听起来不真诚。

definition_zh: 柱子；支柱；栋梁；柱状物；桥墩；门柱
definition_en: a tall upright support of any shape, or a person or thing regarded as essential to a group or system
core_image: 一根方正的立柱顶住门廊，旁边一根圆柱只作装饰；同一词也指撑起整座建筑的那个人
scene: 门廊左侧的方柱已被风雨磨圆了棱角。 The central pillar takes most of the roof's weight, while the others only frame the entrance.
sceneCN: 这里 pillar 指「建筑中直立的支撑柱」（第 1 个义项：柱子、支柱）；句意为中央那根柱子承担屋顶的大部分重量，其余只用来框住入口。图中可辨识物件：门廊、方柱、圆柱、屋顶；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: An upright architectural support
senses.definition: a tall upright support, square or round, often ornamental as well as structural
senses.definitionCN: 高而直立的支撑件，方或圆，常兼具装饰与承重作用
senses.example: A square pillar flanked each side of the porch.
senses.exampleCN: 门廊两侧各立一根方柱。
senses.why: the Latin source meant a pillar of any section, so the word never required the roundness of a classical column.
senses.whyCN: 其拉丁来源指任意截面的柱子，因此这个词从不要求古典柱那样的圆形。

senses.title: A person who holds up a community
senses.definition: a person regarded as a main support of a community or institution
senses.definitionCN: 被视为社区或机构主要支撑的人
senses.example: The old teacher was a pillar of the village for fifty years.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老教师五十年来一直是村里的栋梁。
senses.why: the metaphor is structural and moral at once: remove the person and the group sags.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻同时是结构与道德的：去掉这个人，群体就会塌下去。

senses.title: An essential part of a system
senses.definition: a component on which a system depends, such as a sector of an economy
senses.definitionCN: 某个系统所依赖的组成部分，如经济中的某个部门
senses.example: Tourism is a pillar of the island's income.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业是这座岛屿收入的支柱。
senses.why: systems are described as buildings, so their load-bearing parts are described as pillars.
senses.whyCN: 系统被描述为建筑，因此其承重部分被说成柱子。

senses.title: A tall narrow mass
senses.definition: a tall narrow shape of smoke, light, salt or rock
senses.definitionCN: 烟、光、盐或岩石形成的细高形状
senses.example: A pillar of salt stood where the tide had cut the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水切开的崖边立着一根盐柱。
senses.why: the shape is enough: the word needs no load and no building.
senses.whyCN: 形状就够了：这个词不需要荷载，也不需要建筑。

senses.title: A bridge pier
senses.definition: the vertical support that carries a bridge span
senses.definitionCN: 承托桥梁跨度的竖向支撑
senses.example: The middle pillar of the bridge has been rebuilt twice.
senses.exampleCN: 桥的中墩已重建过两次。
senses.why: engineering uses the plain word for any vertical load path, not only for ornamental shafts.
senses.whyCN: 工程用这个朴素词指任何竖向承重路径，而不只用于装饰柱。

senses.title: A gatepost
senses.definition: a short sturdy post marking or carrying a gate or boundary
senses.definitionCN: 标记或承托门与边界的短粗立柱
senses.example: The gate hangs between two brick pillars.
senses.exampleCN: 大门挂在两根砖柱之间。
senses.why: one of the oldest uses is simply a post that marks a threshold.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法之一就是标记门槛的一根柱子。

senses.title: One of three policy supports
senses.definition: in policy language, one of several coordinated supports of a system, as in pension pillars
senses.definitionCN: 政策语言中某个体系的几根协同支柱之一，如养老金三支柱
senses.example: The report describes the three pillars of the pension scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述该养老金方案的三根支柱。
senses.why: policy analysts borrowed the architectural image to show that the system fails if one support is removed.
senses.whyCN: 政策分析者借用建筑意象，说明抽掉一根支柱体系就会失效。

senses.title: A pillar industry
senses.definition: a sector that carries a large share of a region's output and employment
senses.definitionCN: 承担某地区大部分产出与就业的产业部门
senses.example: Shipbuilding became the pillar of the coastal economy.
senses.exampleCN: 造船业成为沿海经济的支柱。
senses.why: the fixed phrase turns the metaphor into an economic category with measurable weight.
senses.whyCN: 这一固定说法把比喻变成一个有可测分量的经济范畴。

intro.en: Pillar comes from a Latin word for a pillar through Old French, and it has always meant a support of any shape. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pillar 经古法语来自拉丁语中表示「柱子」的词，历来指任意形状的支撑。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pila named a pillar or pier; it is written the same as the word for a ball, and the two are usually treated as separate nouns.
items.cn: pila 指柱子或墩柱；它与表示「球」的词拼写相同，通常被视为两个不同的名词。

items.en: A derived noun pilare named a pillar or a supporting post in later Latin.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语中派生名词 pilare 指柱子或支撑柱。

items.en: Old French pilier carried the word into English, where it named a support in a building or a gate.
items.cn: 古法语 pilier 把这个词带入英语，指建筑或大门中的支撑。

items.en: By the medieval period the word covered bridge piers and gateposts as well as interior shafts.
items.cn: 到中世纪，这个词除室内柱身外还涵盖桥墩与门柱。

items.en: From the sixteenth century a trusted person could be called a pillar of the community or of the church.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，受信赖的人可被称为社区或教会的栋梁。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the ancestry of pila before Latin is not established, and whether it is connected to the ball word is disputed; no shared origin has been demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：pila 在拉丁语之前的谱系未得到证明，它与表示「球」的词是否有联系也有争议；尚无证据显示两者同源。

note.en: Group one holds upright-support words that overlap with pillar; group two holds metaphorical supports and tall masses.
note.cn: 第一组是与 pillar 重叠的直立支撑词；第二组是比喻性支撑与高柱体。

entries.definition: A support, usually round and governed by an order; a pillar may be square and need follow no order.
entries.definitionCN: 通常为圆形且受柱式规范的支撑；pillar 可为方形、无须遵循柱式。

entries.definition: A thick masonry support between openings or under a bridge; it is heavier and more wall-like than a pillar.
entries.definitionCN: 开口之间或桥下的厚砌体支撑；比 pillar 更厚重、更像墙。

entries.definition: A plain upright piece of timber or metal; pillar sounds more monumental and more permanent.
entries.definitionCN: 朴素木制或金属直立件；pillar 听起来更宏大、更持久。

entries.definition: A small pillar; the suffix makes it a minor architectural member.
entries.definitionCN: 小柱子；后缀使它成为次要建筑构件。

entries.definition: The chief support of a system, from a sailing term for the rope holding a mast; it is closer to pillar sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 体系的主要支撑，来自固定桅杆的航海术语；更接近 pillar 的第二个义项。

entries.definition: A support placed under something to hold it up; it is usually temporary and rarely ornamental.
entries.definitionCN: 置于某物下方以托住的支撑，通常临时且少装饰。

entries.definition: Anything that holds weight or sustains a system; it is the neutral term that pillar makes concrete.
entries.definitionCN: 任何承重或维持体系之物；是中性的总称，pillar 使之具体化。

entries.definition: The central strength of a group or system, from the spine; it stresses unity rather than vertical support.
entries.definitionCN: 群体或体系的核心力量，来自脊柱；强调统一性而非竖向支撑。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin source, the real bridge and gate uses, and the real policy phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁来源、真实的桥梁与门柱用法、真实的政策说法。

normal.en: The word never required a round shaft, so a square gatepost is as much a pillar as a marble column.
normal.cn: 这个词从不要求圆形柱身，因此方形门柱与大理石圆柱一样是 pillar。

normal.en: The family runs pillar, pillared, pillaret, pillar-box, pillar-like.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 pillar、pillared、pillaret、pillar-box、pillar-like。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: stone pillar, pillar of society, bridge pillar, pillar industry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：石柱、社会栋梁、桥墩、支柱产业。

normal.en: The metaphor is load-bearing: take the person away and the group sags.
normal.cn: 这个比喻是承重的：把人抽走，群体就会塌。

normal.en: A pillar of salt and a pillar of smoke need no building at all.
normal.cn: 盐柱与烟柱根本不需要建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a village where one person is literally holding up the roof.
abstract.cn: 想象一个村庄里真有一个人托着屋顶。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge standing on one leg in the middle of a river.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥用一条腿立在河心。

abstract.en: Picture a policy report drawn as a temple with three columns.
abstract.cn: 想象一份政策报告被画成一座有三根柱子的神庙。

examples.en: The pillar at the gate carries the date of the first owner.
examples.cn: 门柱上刻着第一任主人的日期。

examples.en: She was a pillar of the hospital's volunteer service.
examples.cn: 她是这家医院志愿服务的栋梁。

examples.en: A pillar of cloud rose over the burning refinery.
examples.cn: 燃烧的炼油厂上方升起一根烟柱。

dict_mnemonic.text: pila（柱子）+ 英语名词尾 → 直立的支撑 → 柱子、支柱、栋梁

root: 古法语 pilier 来自中世纪拉丁 pilare，其源头是拉丁 pila「柱子、墩柱」；英语 pillar。pila 的更早谱系不确定，与表示「球」的 pila 是否有关尚无证据。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one upright piece: a building support becomes a person, a system part, a tall mass, a bridge pier, a gatepost, a policy support and an industry.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一根直立件展开：建筑支撑成为人、体系部件、高柱体、桥墩、门柱、政策支柱与产业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plain upright block that holds something heavier than itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块朴素的直立体，托着比它更重的东西。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL SUPPORT: a shaft, a pier and a gatepost are the same block in three positions.
branches.cn: 实体支撑：柱身、桥墩与门柱，是同一块直立体在三个位置。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a trusted member is described as holding the group up.
branches.cn: 人：受信赖的成员被描述为托住群体的人。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: economic sectors and policy supports are load-bearing parts.
branches.cn: 体系：经济部门与政策支撑都是承重部件。

branches.en: THE MASS: smoke, salt and light keep only the tall narrow shape.
branches.cn: 体量：烟、盐与光只保留了细高的形状。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY: the metaphor hardens into the fixed term pillar industry.
branches.cn: 范畴：比喻固化为「支柱产业」这一固定术语。

intro.en: Pillar is a borrowed noun with almost no productive affix of its own; its family is built with English endings and fixed compounds.
intro.cn: pillar 是借入名词，本身几乎没有能产词缀；其词族由英语词尾与固定复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin pila and the later pilare are the direct sources; English formed pillared and pillaret from the noun, not from new Latin words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pila 与后期的 pilare 是直接来源；英语的 pillared 与 pillaret 是从名词构成，而非新的拉丁词。

items.example: Pilare named the pier of a bridge.
A stone pilier framed the gate.
A pillared porch marks the entrance.
items.exampleCN: 一道有柱的门廊标出入口。

items.example: The red pillar-box stands at the corner.

items.meaning: a sector that carries an economy
items.example: Steel was once a pillar industry here.
items.exampleCN: 钢铁一度是这里的支柱产业。

latinEntries.structure: pilare, pilaris (n., third declension; medieval Latin)

definition_zh: 编织；针织；使紧密结合；接骨愈合
definition_en: to make cloth or a garment by looping yarn with needles, or to join things closely, as a bone or a group may join
core_image: 两根针把一根线一针一针连成一片毛布
scene: 冬夜的沙发上，毛线球慢慢变小。 She sat by the window and knit a scarf while the kettle began to hum.
sceneCN: 这里 knit 是「编织、针织」（第 1 个义项：用针把毛线连成织物），句意是她坐在窗边织围巾，水壶开始响起来。画面里有冬夜的沙发、毛线球与窗。

pos.zh: 动词：编织；针织；使结合；愈合
名词：针织衣物、编织样式

collocations.zh: 一针下、一针上（编织术语）

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「编织、编织物」
加 -er 构成，义为「编织者」
knit 与 wear 合成，义为「针织衣物」
合成形容词，义为「关系紧密的」

senses.title: To make cloth by looping yarn
senses.definition: to make a fabric or garment by interlocking loops of yarn on needles or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 用针或机器把毛线的线圈互相套住，织成织物或衣服
senses.example: Her grandmother knit him a thick woollen hat.
senses.exampleCN: 他奶奶给他织了一顶厚羊毛帽。
senses.why: The core act is joining loops, so that a long single thread becomes a surface.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是接合线圈，使一根长长的单线成为一片面。

senses.title: To join closely together
senses.definition: to unite people or things so closely that they act as one
senses.definitionCN: 把人或事物连得极紧，使其如同一体
senses.example: Shared hardship had knit the team together.
senses.exampleCN: 共同的艰难把队伍紧紧连在一起。
senses.why: Because knitting makes separate loops into one surface, the word easily describes people joined in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 因为编织把一个个分开的线圈连成一整片，这个词很自然地用来描述同样结合的人。

senses.title: To heal and join, of a bone
senses.definition: of a broken bone, to grow back together and become whole again
senses.definitionCN: 指断骨重新长合，恢复完整
senses.example: The broken rib will knit in about six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 断掉的肋骨大约六周就能长合。
senses.why: A healing bone closes the same way cloth does, thread by thread, so medicine borrowed the weaver word.
senses.whyCN: 愈合的骨头像布一样一针一针合拢，医学便借用了织工的词。

senses.title: To draw brows together
senses.definition: to draw the eyebrows closely together, usually in worry or thought
senses.definitionCN: 多因忧虑或思考把眉毛挤在一起
senses.example: He knit his brows at the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 他读信时皱起了眉。
senses.why: Drawing brows together is the same gesture of closing a gap, so the weaving word serves for the face.
senses.whyCN: 把眉毛挤在一处正是在闭合缝隙，于是织工的词也用到了脸上。

intro.en: Knit comes from an Old English verb for tying a knot, and its meaning shifted from knotting to looping yarn.
intro.cn: knit 源自古英语表示「打结」的动词，词义由打结转为把毛线绕成线圈。

items.en: The verb cnyttan meant to tie or fasten with a knot, often used of nets and snares.
items.cn: 动词 cnyttan 意为打结、系扎，常用于网与陷阱。

items.en: The related German knoten and Dutch knopen keep the knot sense in the modern languages.
items.cn: 相关的德语 knoten 与荷兰语 knopen 在现代语言里仍保留打结义。

items.en: In Middle English the word could already mean both tying and forming loops of yarn.
items.cn: 到中古英语时，这个词已同时指打结与绕成线圈。

items.en: The looped-cloth sense wins, and the older knot sense survives in the related word knot.
items.cn: 绕线圈的布料义胜出，打结义则留在相关的 knot 一词里。

items.en: Metaphors spread: bones knit, teams knit, and people speak of a close-knit family.
items.cn: 比喻四处扩展：骨能长合，队伍能连紧，人们也说起 close-knit 的家庭。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers silent-k words close to knit; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of making cloth or joining things.
note.cn: 形近组收与 knit 接近的 k 不发音词；近义组收其他织布或连接的方式。

entries.definition: The knot word from the same Old English root, now naming the tied loop.
entries.definitionCN: 同出古英语词根的「结」，如今指系出的绳结。

entries.definition: Starts with the same silent k and names a mounted warrior.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以不发音的 k 开头，指骑士。

entries.definition: Missing the k, and names the egg of a louse.
To cross threads lengthwise and widthwise on a loom, unlike the loops of knitting.
entries.definitionCN: 在织机上经纬交错，与针织的绕圈不同。

entries.definition: To make cloth with a single hooked needle.
entries.definitionCN: 用一支带钩的针做织品。

entries.definition: To join cloth with thread and a needle by stitching.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real knot origin, the two past forms, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的「打结」来源、两种过去式，以及这个词常见的搭配。

normal.en: The oldest sense is to tie a knot, which is why knot and knit are relatives.
normal.cn: 最古老的意思是打结，所以 knot 与 knit 是亲属。

normal.en: British English prefers knitted; American English also uses knit as the past.
normal.cn: 英式英语偏好 knitted，美式英语也把 knit 用作过去式。

normal.en: Knit doubles the t before -ed and -ing: knitted, knitting.
normal.cn: knit 在加 -ed、-ing 前要双写 t：knitted、knitting。

normal.en: Knit together is the everyday metaphor for a united group.
normal.cn: knit together 是与团结相关的日常比喻。

normal.en: Close-knit describes a family or team that holds together tightly.
normal.cn: close-knit 描述紧密相依的家庭或团队。

abstract.en: One thread is weak; thousands of loops make a fabric that holds the body warm.
abstract.cn: 一根线脆弱，几千个线圈却能织成一面裹住身体的布。

abstract.en: Knitting is a slow addition: each loop shrinks the distance to a finished thing.
abstract.cn: 编织是缓慢的加法：每一个线圈都缩短了与成品的距离。

abstract.en: A bone joins and a friendship joins in the same verb, because both close a gap loop by loop.
abstract.cn: 骨头长合与友谊结合用同一个动词，因为二者都是一圈一圈地闭合缝隙。

examples.en: She knits while listening to the radio.
examples.cn: 她边听收音机边编织。

examples.en: The small village is a close-knit community.
examples.cn: 这个小村子是一个关系紧密的社区。

examples.en: The two bones knitted cleanly within two months.
examples.cn: 两块骨头在两个月内干净地长合了。

dict_mnemonic.text: knit 原是打结，一针一针打下去就成了织物

root: 古英语 cnyttan「打结、系扎」，与 knot 同源，同出于日耳曼语；中古英语兼指打结与绕线，现代英语以「针织」为主义，并引申出结合、愈合、皱眉等义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: making cloth from loops, joining people closely, a bone healing together, and drawing the brows together.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：用线圈织成布，把人紧密连起，骨头长合，以及把眉毛挤在一起。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two needles pulling one thread into a chain of loops that becomes cloth.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根针把一根线拉成一串线圈，最终成为布。

branches.en: THE CLOTH LINE: interlocking loops turn one thread into a surface.
branches.cn: 布料线：互相套住的线圈把一根线变成一片面。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE LINE: close relations are described with the weaver word.
branches.cn: 人际线：紧密的关系用织工的词来描述。

branches.en: THE BONE LINE: medicine borrowed the verb for joining broken parts.
branches.cn: 骨线：医学借这个动词表示接合断处。

branches.en: THE FACE LINE: brows drawn together repeat the closing of a gap.
branches.cn: 面部线：把眉毛挤在一起，重复了闭合缝隙的动作。

branches.en: THE KNOT LINE: the oldest sense survives in the related word knot.
branches.cn: 结线：最古老的意思留在相关的 knot 一词里。

intro.en: Knit is a native Germanic verb; English extends it with suffixes and compounds such as knitwear.
intro.cn: knit 是本族日耳曼动词，英语用后缀与 knitwear 一类合成来扩展它。

latinIntro.en: Knit has no Latin ancestor, so the Latin joining words here serve only as comparisons.
latinIntro.cn: knit 没有拉丁语祖先，这里的拉丁语连接词只作对照。

items.example: Her knitting is on the chair.

items.exampleCN: 这是一支紧密团结的队伍。
他们把俱乐部紧紧凝聚在一起。

definition_zh: 撤退；退却；退缩；隐居处
definition_en: to move back or away from danger, or a quiet place to rest
core_image: 队伍收起旗帜，沿着来路悄悄向后移动
scene: 敌军在夜色中撤退，留下了空荡荡的营地。 The enemy retreated under cover of darkness, leaving an empty camp.
sceneCN: 这里 retreat 是「撤退」（第 1 个义项：因不利情况而后退）；句意：敌军在夜色中撤退，留下了空荡荡的营地。

senses.title: Move back from danger
senses.definition: to move away from an enemy or a dangerous situation
senses.definitionCN: 从敌人或危险处境中后撤
senses.example: The soldiers retreated to the river.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们撤退到河边。
senses.why: The French source means to draw back, so retreat is a deliberate backward movement.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为往回拉，因此 retreat 是有意的后撤。

senses.title: Avoid a difficult situation
senses.definition: to move away from something difficult or frightening
senses.definitionCN: 从困难或可怕的事物前退开
senses.example: He retreated from the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 他从争论中退缩了。
senses.why: Physical withdrawal becomes a way of avoiding conflict.
senses.whyCN: 身体上的后撤变成了回避冲突的方式。

senses.title: A quiet private place
senses.definition: a quiet place where people go to rest or pray
senses.definitionCN: 人们去休息或祈祷的安静之处
senses.example: The monks live in a mountain retreat.
senses.exampleCN: 僧侣们住在山中的静修处。
senses.why: A place to which one withdraws takes the name of the withdrawal.
senses.whyCN: 人们退隐前往的地方，就取了「退隐」这个名字。

intro.en: Retreat comes from Old French retret, from retraire, to draw back.
intro.cn: retreat 源自古法语 retret，来自 retraire（往回拉）。

items.en: Retrahere means to draw back.
items.cn: retrahere 意为往回拉。

items.en: Retraire means to withdraw.
items.cn: retraire 意为撤退。

items.en: Retret means a withdrawal.
items.cn: retret 意为撤退。

items.en: Retreat names military withdrawal.
items.cn: retreat 指军事撤退。

items.en: It also names quiet places for rest.
items.cn: 它也指安静的休养之地。

note.en: Retreat is close to withdraw and retire, with a military flavor.
note.cn: retreat 与撤退、退下相近，带有军事色彩。

entries.definition: moving back
the habit of avoiding action
to deal with someone
to move away from a place
to move back from an enemy
a place of safety

normalIntro.en: Retreat is a rope pulled back: the line moves away from danger.
normalIntro.cn: retreat 就像被拉回的绳子：战线远离危险。

normal.en: Retreat from battle means leave the fighting.
normal.cn: retreat from battle 意为离开战斗。

normal.en: Beat a retreat means hurry away.
normal.cn: beat a retreat 意为匆忙退走。

normal.en: A quiet retreat is a peaceful place to rest.
normal.cn: a quiet retreat 是安静的休养地。

normal.en: Retreat into oneself means become withdrawn.
normal.cn: retreat into oneself 意为变得封闭。

normal.en: Compare withdraw: withdraw is neutral, retreat often suggests pressure.
normal.cn: 对比 withdraw：withdraw 较中性，retreat 常暗示压力。

abstract.en: Picture a tide pulling back from the shore.
abstract.cn: 想象潮水从岸边退去。

abstract.en: Imagine a flag lowered and carried away.
abstract.cn: 想象旗帜被降下带走。

abstract.en: Think of a small house hidden among trees.
abstract.cn: 想象树丛中隐蔽的小屋。

examples.en: The army retreated after a long battle.
examples.cn: 经过长时间战斗，军队撤退了。

examples.en: She retreated to her room to think.
examples.cn: 她退回房间思考。

examples.en: They spent the weekend at a country retreat.
examples.cn: 他们在一个乡间静修处度周末。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ treat（对待）」——先把自己往回带，就是撤退；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ trahere（拉）→ retrahere（往回拉）→ 古法语 retret → retreat，核心义「向后撤、退开」。

sensesIntro.en: Retreat first means move back from danger, then avoid a hard situation, and finally names the quiet place one withdraws to.
sensesIntro.cn: retreat 先指从危险中后撤，再指回避困难处境，最后指退隐前往的安静之处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of soldiers moving quietly backward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队士兵悄悄向后移动。

branches.en: Military withdrawal is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 军事撤退是基本义。

branches.en: Avoiding conflict is retreat in daily life.
branches.cn: 回避冲突是日常生活中的退缩。

branches.en: The place of withdrawal becomes a retreat.
branches.cn: 退隐之处成为一个静修地。

branches.en: Both battle lines and arguments can be left.
branches.cn: 战线与争论都可以退出。

branches.en: Retreating to a quiet place restores strength.
branches.cn: 退到安静之处能恢复力量。

intro.en: Retreat is built on Latin re- and trahere, to draw.
intro.cn: retreat 建立在拉丁语 re- 与 trahere（拉）之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin retrahere means to draw back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 retrahere 意为往回拉。

items.example: Old French retraire carries the word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 retraire 传递了该词。

definition_zh: 家庭教师；导师；辅导
definition_en: a teacher who works with one student or a small group, or to teach in this way
core_image: 书桌两侧对坐的两个人，一个讲一道题，一个握笔在算
scene: 放学后的图书馆角落，两名学生隔着桌子低声讨论数学。 His tutor showed him a shorter way to solve the equation.
sceneCN: 这里 tutor 是「家庭教师；导师」（第 1 个义项：单独或小班辅导学生的老师）；句意为他的导师教他一种更短的解题方法。两人隔着书桌对坐的画面，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由 tutor 加 -ial 构成，义为「辅导课」
由同一拉丁词根构成，义为「学费；教学」
由 tutor 加 -ing 构成，义为「辅导工作」

senses.title: The one beside you
senses.definition: a teacher who gives lessons to one learner or a small group
senses.definitionCN: 给一名学生或一小群人单独授课的老师
senses.example: His tutor showed him a shorter way to solve the equation.
senses.exampleCN: 他的导师教他一种更短的解题方法。
senses.why: A tutor is close enough to watch one person think, which is what separates the role from a class teacher.
senses.whyCN: 家教近到能看着一个人思考，这正是它区别于班级教师的地方。

senses.title: The guide at college
senses.definition: a member of staff who advises a student on study and progress
senses.definitionCN: 在大学里就学业与进度指导学生的工作人员
senses.example: Every first-year student is assigned a tutor.
senses.exampleCN: 每位一年级学生都分配一位导师。
senses.why: The university kept the word for the person who guards a student's course, not just one subject.
senses.whyCN: 大学保留这个词，指照看学生整个课程而不只是某一科的人。

senses.title: The act of guiding
senses.definition: to teach one person or a few people, often outside school
senses.definitionCN: 常在校外对一人或数人进行教学
senses.example: She tutors two children in reading on Saturdays.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周六给两个孩子辅导阅读。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: to be the tutor is to do what a tutor does.
senses.whyCN: 名词转动词：当导师就是做导师该做的事。

intro.en: Tutor comes from Latin tueri, to watch over, the same root as tutelage and tuition.
intro.cn: tutor 来自拉丁语 tueri（看守、守护），与 tutelage、tuition 同根。

items.en: Tueri meant to look after or guard someone or something.
items.cn: tueri 意为照看、守护某人或某物。

items.en: Tutor named the guardian, the one who watches over another.
items.cn: tutor 指守护者，即看护他人的人。

items.en: French carried tutor in the sense of a legal guardian.
items.cn: 法语传入 tutor 时带有法定监护人的意思。

items.en: English used it for a guardian before it became a word for a teacher.
items.cn: 英语先把它用作监护人，后来才转为教师。

items.en: The teaching sense won: the one who guards a learner now guards the learning.
items.cn: 教学义胜出：守护学习者的人，如今守护的是学习本身。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root, the second names other teaching roles.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词根，第二组是其他教学角色。

entries.definition: A small teaching session.
Teaching, or the fee for it.
The care of a guardian or teacher.
A person who teaches a class.
An experienced adviser.
A trainer who prepares someone.

normalIntro.en: Tutor keeps the old meaning of guarding: the teacher who watches over one learner.
normalIntro.cn: tutor 保留着守护的古义：盯着一个学生学的老师。

normal.en: Tutor, tuition and tutelage all start from the same Latin watch.
normal.cn: tutor、tuition、tutelage 都起自同一个拉丁语的「看」。

normal.en: The British stress is on the first syllable, the American one is closer to too.
normal.cn: 英式重音在前，美式首元音近于 too。

normal.en: As a verb it takes an object and often in: tutor him in maths.
normal.cn: 作动词时常接 in：tutor him in maths。

normal.en: A tutor teaches one, a class teacher teaches many.
normal.cn: 家教教一个，班级教师教一群。

normal.en: Tutorial is the session, tutor is the person.
normal.cn: tutorial 是课，tutor 是人。

abstract.en: Two chairs pulled close to one desk.
abstract.cn: 两把椅子拉到同一张桌子旁。

abstract.en: A pencil marking the same sum a second time.
abstract.cn: 一支铅笔把同一道题再标一遍。

abstract.en: A lamp left on over a late page.
abstract.cn: 深夜仍亮在某页书上的灯。

examples.en: Her parents found a tutor for the final term.
examples.cn: 她父母为最后一个学期请了家教。

examples.en: He tutors village children in maths for free.
examples.cn: 他免费给村里的孩子辅导数学。

examples.en: My tutor asked whether I had chosen a topic yet.
examples.cn: 我的导师问我是否已经选好题目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「兔特」——老师像盯着兔子一样盯着一个学生学，就是家教。

root: 源自中古英语 tutour、古法语 tutor，上溯拉丁语 tutor（守护者）与动词 tueri（看守），本义为看护学习的人，同族词有 tuition、tutorial、tutelage。

sensesIntro.en: First the teacher who sits beside one learner, then the university guide, then the act of doing that work.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是坐在一个学生旁边的老师，再是大学里的导师，最后是做这件事本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two chairs drawn up to one desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：两把椅子拉到同一张桌边。

branches.en: The near teacher branch: one desk, one learner.
branches.cn: 近身教师分支：一桌一学生。

branches.en: The guardian branch: the college keeps the old watch.
branches.cn: 守护分支：大学保留了古老的看护。

branches.en: The act branch: doing what the guardian does.
branches.cn: 动作分支：做守护者所做的事。

branches.en: The lesson branch: the desk is where both meet.
branches.cn: 功课分支：书桌是双方相遇之处。

branches.en: The study branch: progress is followed week by week.
branches.cn: 学业分支：进度被一周周跟进。

intro.en: Tutor is a Latin agent form, and the family grows with -ial and -ion.
intro.cn: tutor 是拉丁语的施动形式，词族靠 -ial、-ion 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb tueri, to watch over, supplies the whole family, listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 tueri（看守）供应了整个词族，列在下面。

items.example: He tutored her for a year.

definition_zh: 可选的；非强制的；选修的
definition_en: not required, but left to a person's own choice; offered as an extra that may be taken or left
core_image: 一张报名表上，几行字旁印着小星号，其余空格留白等人自行决定
scene: 报名表摊在桌上，几行字旁印着小小的星号，其余空格留白，等人自己决定填不填。 The extra lesson is optional, so nobody has to stay after class.
sceneCN: 这里 optional 是「可选的、非强制的」（第 1 个义项：由本人自行决定是否做）；句意为加课可以自由参加，没人必须课后留下，画面是摊开的报名表与小小的星号。

pos.zh: 可选的；非强制的；选修的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 optio（选择）经古法语 option 进入英语，义为「选项；选择权」
由 optional 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「可选地；非强制地」
由拉丁语 optare（选择）经法语进入英语，义为「选择；挑选」
由 optional 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可选性」

senses.title: Not required but allowed
senses.definition: available to be done or taken if one wishes, but not demanded by any rule
senses.definitionCN: 想做或想取用便可做、可取用，但并不由任何规则强制要求
senses.example: Attendance at the evening talk is optional.
senses.exampleCN: 晚上的讲座可以自愿参加。
senses.why: Latin optio named a choice, so the adjective simply marks something that sits among options rather than among duties.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 optio 指「选择」，所以这个形容词只是标明某事列在选项之中，而不在义务之列；重点落在「可以挑」。

senses.title: Offered as an extra that may be added
senses.titleCN: 作为额外附加、可加可不加的
senses.definition: supplied in addition to what is basic or necessary, so that a person may add it or leave it out
senses.definitionCN: 在基本或必需的内容之外额外提供，可以添上，也可以略去
senses.example: The suitcase comes with an optional strap for long walks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个箱子配有一条可选背带，走远路时可以用。
senses.why: Once a thing is one of the options, it can be offered beside the main item, and the word shifts from permission to a purchasable extra.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西既然位列选项，就可以摆在主件旁边额外提供，词义便从「允许」转到「可添置的附加项」，决定权仍在使用者手里。

senses.title: Chosen rather than compulsory, of a school subject
senses.definition: describing a course or subject that a student may choose instead of a required one
senses.definitionCN: 形容学生可以自行选择、而非必修的课程或科目
senses.example: She took two optional courses in her second year.
senses.exampleCN: 她在二年级选了两门选修课。
senses.why: In a curriculum the choice becomes visible as a list of subjects, and optional marks the ones a student may pick up or pass by.
senses.whyCN: 在课程表里，「选择」变成一张科目清单，optional 标出那些可以选上、也可以略过的科目；这是选择在教育场景中的具体落点。

intro.en: Optional is option plus the adjective ending -al; option goes back through French to a Latin noun for choice.
intro.cn: optional 是 option 加形容词词尾 -al；option 则经法语上溯到表示「选择」的拉丁名词。

items.en: Optio meant a choice or the power of choosing, and it could also name a person chosen for a duty.
items.cn: optio 指选择或选择权，也可指被选出来担任某项事务的人。

items.en: The verb optare meant to choose or to wish, and it stands behind the whole English family.
items.cn: 动词 optare 意为选择、盼望，是整个英语词族的源头。

items.en: Old French option kept the sense of a choice between possibilities and passed it into English.
items.cn: 古法语 option 保留「在多种可能中作选择」的意思，并传入英语。

items.en: English took option as a noun of choice, and by the seventeenth century optional marked what was left to choice.
items.cn: 英语以 option 作表示选择的名词，到十七世纪 optional 用来标明「交由选择决定」的事物。

items.en: Modern English uses optional for forms, features, courses and extras that nobody is obliged to take.
items.cn: 现代英语用 optional 指表格项、功能、课程与附加物中无人必须接受的部分。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin root for choosing and a spelling that only resembles them; the near-meaning group gathers words for what is left to free will.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「选择」词根上的词，以及只是拼写相近的一个词；近义组收表示「交由自由意愿」的词。

entries.definition: A thing that may be chosen, or the right to choose.
entries.definitionCN: 可供选择的事物，或选择的权利。

entries.definition: To choose one thing rather than another.
In a way that is not required.
entries.definitionCN: 以非强制、可选择的方式。

entries.definition: A person who makes or sells glasses; the opening letters resemble option, but the word comes from Greek for sight and is unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 制作或出售眼镜的人；开头拼写像 option，但词源是希腊语「看」，只是拼写相近，来源不同。

entries.definition: Done by one's own wish rather than by obligation.
entries.definitionCN: 出于自愿而非义务去做的。

entries.definition: Chosen by a student rather than required, as of a course.
entries.definitionCN: 由学生选择而非必修的，如课程。

entries.definition: Left to someone's judgment or free decision.
entries.definitionCN: 交由某人判断或自由决定的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a choice-noun wearing an adjective ending, so its hooks all turn on who holds the decision.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是穿着形容词词尾的「选择」名词，记忆钩子都围绕「决定权在谁手里」。

normal.en: Option means a choice, and optional adds -al, so the word describes what choice is allowed to reach.
normal.cn: option 意为选择，optional 加 -al，所以这个词描述的是「选择所能触及的范围」。

normal.en: The ending -al turns a noun of choice into an adjective of permission rather than of command.
normal.cn: 词尾 -al 把表示选择的名词变成表示许可的形容词，而不是表示命令的形容词。

normal.en: Optional course and optional extra follow the same logic: the item is there, but the decision is yours.
normal.cn: optional course 与 optional extra 逻辑相同：东西摆在那里，决定权归你。

normal.en: English often adds entirely to optional to stress that no hidden rule stands behind the offer.
normal.cn: 英语常在 optional 前加 entirely，强调这份好意背后没有藏着任何硬性规定。

normal.en: Optional does not mean unimportant; it means not required, and the difference is worth keeping.
normal.cn: optional 不等于不重要，它只表示不作要求，这个区别值得守住。

abstract.en: An asterisk beside a line on a form is a small sign that says this blank is yours to fill or leave.
abstract.cn: 表格行旁的小星号是个小小提示：这一格填或不填都由你。

abstract.en: A menu with a page of add-ons keeps the meal complete without them, and optional is that extra page.
abstract.cn: 一份另附加页的菜单，不加也吃得完整，optional 就是那页附加内容。

abstract.en: A path that splits, one side marked required and one side open, is the word drawn as a choice on the ground.
abstract.cn: 一条分岔的路，一边写着必须，一边空着，就是这个词画在地上的样子。

examples.en: The extra lesson is optional, so nobody has to stay after class.
examples.cn: 加课可以自由参加，没人必须课后留下。

examples.en: The suitcase comes with an optional strap for long walks.
examples.cn: 这个箱子配有一条可选背带，走远路时可以用。

examples.en: She took two optional courses in her second year.
examples.cn: 她在二年级选了两门选修课。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我普选」——普选就是人人可挑可弃；optional 意为可选的。

root: 拉丁语 optio（选择）→ 古法语 option → 英语 option（选项；选择权），加形容词后缀 -al 构成 optional，意为「交由本人选择的」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a choice left open; the senses move from permission, to an add-on that may be taken, to a subject a student may pick.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「留着不定的选择」；义项从许可，转到可添可不添的附加物，再落到学生可以挑选的科目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a form with small asterisks beside a few lines, the rest left blank for the writer to decide.
core.cn: 核心意象：表格上几行字旁的小星号，其余空格留给填表人自行决定。

branches.en: a form line marked with an asterisk
branches.cn: 表格上一行带星号的字

branches.en: a strap offered beside a suitcase
branches.cn: 箱子旁另配的一条背带

branches.en: two courses picked from a long list
branches.cn: 从长清单里挑出的两门课

branches.en: one permission, once for a blank and once for an add-on
branches.cn: 同一种许可，一次落在空格上，一次落在附加物上

branches.en: a decision made inside a curriculum
branches.cn: 在课程表之内作出的决定

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin noun and verb for choosing, with an English adjective ending and a small family of derived forms.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「选择」的拉丁名词与动词构成，外加一个英语形容词词尾和一小族派生形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 黏土；陶土；（网球）红土场地
definition_en: heavy sticky earth that can be shaped when wet and baked hard, or a sports surface made of crushed clay
core_image: 转盘上被手指拉高的湿泥坯
scene: 轮盘转起来，手上沾满湿乎乎的土。 She pressed a lump of clay into a shallow bowl.
sceneCN: 这里 clay 指「黏土」（第 1 个义项：湿时可塑、烧后变硬的黏性土）；句意是她把一团黏土按成了一个浅碗。

senses.title: Sticky earth for shaping
senses.definition: a heavy sticky earth that becomes soft when wet and hard when baked
senses.definitionCN: 湿时变软、烧后变硬的厚重黏性土
senses.example: The children shaped animals from clay.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们用黏土捏动物。
senses.why: The old English word named exactly this sticky earth, and that sense has never changed.
senses.whyCN: 古英语中的这个词正是指这种黏性土，这一含义从未改变。

senses.title: A crushed-clay sports surface
senses.definition: a tennis court surface made of crushed brick or clay
senses.definitionCN: 用碎砖或黏土铺成的网球场地面
senses.example: He plays best on clay.
senses.exampleCN: 他在红土场上打得最好。
senses.why: Players shortened the name of the clay court until the material alone meant the surface.
senses.whyCN: 球员把红土球场的名称缩短，最后材料名本身就指这种场地。

intro.en: Clay is a native English word for sticky earth, with relatives across the Germanic languages.
intro.cn: clay 是英语本族词，指黏性土，在日耳曼诸语言中有同源词。

items.en: Clæg meant sticky earth used by potters.
items.cn: clæg 指陶工使用的黏性土。

items.en: The spelling settled as clay.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 clay。

items.en: Writers used clay for the human body in religious prose.
items.cn: 作家在宗教文章中用 clay 指人的身体。

items.en: Brick and tile works made clay a trade word.
items.cn: 砖瓦业使 clay 成为行业词。

items.en: Sports also gave the word a surface sense.
items.cn: 体育又给了这个词场地义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words with a similar vowel or ending, while the meaning group names kinds of earth.
note.cn: 形近组列出元音或结尾相近的短词，近义组列出各种泥土。

entries.definition: to become too sweet or too much
to kill someone or something
a sharp curved nail
wet earth that sticks to your shoes
the top layer of earth where plants grow
the substance of the ground

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the potter's wheel, the brick kiln and the red court.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用陶轮、砖窑与红土球场。

normal.en: Clay is what a potter's hands are covered with at the end of the day.
normal.cn: clay 就是陶艺师收工时满手沾着的东西。

normal.en: Wet clay bends, dry clay cracks, fired clay rings.
normal.cn: 湿黏土会弯，干黏土会裂，烧过的陶会响。

normal.en: Clay and clod share a shape and both mean lumpy earth.
normal.cn: clay 与 clod 外形相近，都指成块的土。

normal.en: A clay court is red because crushed brick is mixed in.
normal.cn: 红土球场之所以发红，是因为掺了碎砖。

normal.en: Clay is uncountable, so one says a lump of clay.
normal.cn: clay 不可数，所以说 a lump of clay。

abstract.en: Picture a wet grey cylinder rising under two fingers on a spinning wheel.
abstract.cn: 想象转盘上湿灰的泥柱在两根手指间升高。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of unglazed pots drying in the shade.
abstract.cn: 想象架子上摆着一排未上釉的陶罐在阴处晾干。

abstract.en: Picture a red tennis court with white lines and a sliding player.
abstract.cn: 想象一片画着白线的红土球场，一名球员正在滑步。

examples.en: The children shaped animals from clay.
examples.cn: 孩子们用黏土捏动物。

examples.en: She pressed a lump of clay into a shallow bowl.
examples.cn: 她把一团黏土按成了一个浅碗。

examples.en: He plays best on clay in the spring.
examples.cn: 春天他在红土场上打得最好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cl 想成「粘」，ay 想成「哎」：粘手得让人哎一声的土，就是黏土。

root: 源自古英语 clæg（黏性土、陶土），与荷兰语 klei、德语 Klei 同源，本义一直保持至今。

sensesIntro.en: Sticky earth for pots first, then the crushed material that makes a court surface.
sensesIntro.cn: 先指做陶器的黏性土，再指铺球场的那种碎料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet clay cylinder rising on a potter's wheel.
core.cn: 核心意象：陶轮上湿黏土被拉高的圆柱。

branches.en: Sticky earth is shaped by hands and then baked.
branches.cn: 黏性土被手塑形，再经火烧。

branches.en: Crushed clay becomes a sports surface.
branches.cn: 碎黏土成了运动场地。

branches.en: The material sense underlies the surface sense.
branches.cn: 材料义是场地义的基础。

branches.en: Pottery, bricks and tiles all begin with this word.
branches.cn: 陶器、砖与瓦都从这个词开始。

branches.en: The court is named by what it is made of.
branches.cn: 这种场地以它的材料命名。

intro.en: The noun takes a plural-free form and grows two derived words.
intro.cn: 这个名词没有复数形式，只长出两个派生词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base: clay is a native Germanic word.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语词基：clay 是日耳曼语本族词。

items.exampleCN: 这部影片用了黏土动画。

items.meaning: a pot made of baked clay
items.example: The clay pot keeps the water cool.

items.meaning: soil with a lot of clay in it

definition_zh: 加仑（容量单位）；一加仑的量；大量
definition_en: a unit for measuring liquid, about four and a half litres in Britain or about three point eight litres in the United States
core_image: 一大桶牛奶上标着容量刻度
scene: 他买了一加仑牛奶带回家。 He bought a gallon of milk and took it home.
sceneCN: 这里 gallon 是「加仑」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他买了一加仑牛奶带回家。

senses.title: Unit of liquid measure
senses.definition: a unit for measuring liquid, with different sizes in Britain and America
senses.definitionCN: 测量液体的单位，在英国和美国大小不同
senses.example: He bought a gallon of milk and took it home.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了一加仑牛奶带回家。
senses.why: This is the standard measuring sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是标准的计量义项。

senses.title: Amount held by one gallon
senses.definition: the amount of liquid that fills a gallon container
senses.definitionCN: 装满一加仑容器所需的液体量
senses.example: The engine used half a gallon on the short trip.
senses.exampleCN: 这段短途行程发动机用了半加仑。
senses.why: The unit also names the quantity itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个单位也指数量本身。

senses.title: A great deal
senses.definition: a very large amount, used informally in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用语，复数形式表示非常大的量
senses.example: Gallons of water poured through the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 大量的水从屋顶灌下来。
senses.why: The container size became a picture of plenty.
senses.whyCN: 容器的容量变成了「很多」的形象。

intro.en: Gallon came from Old Northern French, naming a measure of liquid.
intro.cn: gallon 来自古北法语，原指一种液体容量单位。

items.en: Galon named a liquid measure.
items.cn: galon 指一种液体容量单位。

items.en: English borrowed the word as gallon.
items.cn: 英语把它借入为 gallon。

items.en: Britain and America fixed different sizes.
items.cn: 英国和美国确定了不同的大小。

items.en: It also names a large container.
items.cn: 它也指大型容器。

items.en: In speech, gallons can mean a great deal.
items.cn: 在口语中，gallons 可以表示很多。

note.en: Gallon is compared with look-alike words and other units of volume.
note.cn: 把 gallon 与形近词以及其他容量单位作比较。
