examples.en: This car does forty miles per gallon.
examples.cn: 这辆车每加仑能跑四十英里。

dict_mnemonic.text: gallon 与 gallery、gallop 形近；a gallon of 是「一加仑的」，miles per gallon 是「每加仑英里数」。

root: 经古北法语 galon 进入英语，核心义「量液体的容量单位」。

sensesIntro.en: Gallon is a liquid measure, the amount it holds, or informally a great deal.
sensesIntro.cn: gallon 是液体容量单位、其所盛的量，或口语中的大量。

core.en: A fixed amount used to measure liquid.
core.cn: 用来测量液体的固定容量。

branches.en: Milk is sold by the gallon.
branches.cn: 牛奶按加仑出售。

branches.en: Half a gallon feeds a short journey.
branches.cn: 半加仑足以支撑一段短途。

branches.en: Water falls in impossible amounts.
branches.cn: 水以惊人的量落下。

branches.en: The unit and the amount are one idea.
branches.cn: 单位与数量是同一个概念。

branches.en: A full container suggests plenty.
branches.cn: 满容器暗示富足。

intro.en: Gallon forms words for measures and containers.
intro.cn: gallon 构成表示计量和容器的词。

latinIntro.en: Gallon came through Old French rather than Latin.
latinIntro.cn: gallon 经古法语传来，而非拉丁语。

items.example: The bill lists the gallonage used.
items.exampleCN: 账单列出了用水的加仑数。

items.example: The cider came in a gallon jug.
items.exampleCN: 苹果酒装在一加仑的壶里。
他买了一个一加仑大的瓶子。

items.example: The farmer used a gallon measure.
items.exampleCN: 农夫用了一个加仑量器。

definition_zh: 磨碎；碾碎；磨（牙）；苦干
definition_en: to crush something into small pieces or powder
core_image: 石磨缓缓转动，麦粒变成面粉
scene: 她把咖啡豆磨成细粉。 She ground the coffee beans into powder.
sceneCN: 这里 grind 是「磨碎」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把咖啡豆磨成细粉。

senses.title: Crush into powder
senses.definition: to crush something into small pieces or powder
senses.definitionCN: 把某物碾成小块或粉末
senses.example: She ground the coffee beans into powder.
senses.exampleCN: 她把咖啡豆磨成细粉。
senses.why: The physical crushing is the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 物理的碾磨是这个词的核心。

senses.title: Rub the teeth
senses.definition: to rub the upper and lower teeth together
senses.definitionCN: 上下牙齿相互摩擦
senses.example: He grinds his teeth at night.
senses.exampleCN: 他夜里磨牙。
senses.why: The same rubbing motion moves to the jaw.
senses.whyCN: 同样的摩擦动作转移到牙关。

senses.title: Work long and hard
senses.definition: to work slowly and steadily at something hard
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢而持续地做艰苦的事
senses.example: They grind away at the same task.
senses.exampleCN: 他们日复一日地苦干同一件事。
senses.why: Endless work is felt as a mill turning.
senses.whyCN: 无休止的工作，被感受为不停转动的磨。

intro.en: Grind is an Old English verb for crushing grain.
intro.cn: grind 是古英语动词，指把谷物磨碎。

items.en: Grindan meant to crush or grind.
items.cn: grindan 意为碾碎、磨碎。

items.en: Grind kept the mill and grain sense.
items.cn: grind 保留磨坊与谷物的含义。

items.en: It extended to teeth and to hard work.
items.cn: 词义扩展到磨牙与苦干。

items.en: Grind to a halt described a slow stop.
items.cn: grind to a halt 形容慢慢停下。

items.en: The daily grind named routine labor.
items.cn: the daily grind 指日常的苦差。

note.en: Grind is compared with look-alike words and words for crushing.
note.cn: 把 grind 与形近词以及表示碾碎的词作比较。

entries.definition: large and impressive
of the colour of grass
to smile widely
to press until broken
to grind grain
to reduce to powder

normalIntro.en: Grind is stone against grain, day after day.
normalIntro.cn: grind 是石头对着谷物，日复一日。

normal.en: Grind the pepper finely.
normal.cn: 把胡椒磨细。

normal.en: The mill grinds wheat.
normal.cn: 磨坊磨小麦。

normal.en: He grinds his teeth in sleep.
normal.cn: 他睡觉时磨牙。

normal.en: The machine ground to a halt.
normal.cn: 机器慢慢停了下来。

normal.en: She hates the daily grind.
normal.cn: 她讨厌日常的苦差。

abstract.en: The mill does not hurry, yet it finishes.
abstract.cn: 磨不着急，却总能磨完。

abstract.en: What is ground fine disappears into bread.
abstract.cn: 磨细的东西，消失在面包里。

abstract.en: Patience is a slow stone.
abstract.cn: 耐心，是一块转得慢的石头。

examples.en: She ground the coffee beans into powder.
examples.cn: 她把咖啡豆磨成细粉。

examples.en: He grinds his teeth at night.
examples.cn: 他夜里磨牙。

examples.en: They grind away at the same task.
examples.cn: 他们日复一日地苦干同一件事。

dict_mnemonic.text: grind 的过去式和过去分词都是 ground；grind coffee 是磨咖啡，grind one's teeth 是磨牙，the daily grind 是日常苦差，grind to a halt 是慢慢停下。

root: 来自古英语 grindan（碾碎），核心义为石头对谷物的研磨，后扩展到磨牙、机器停转与辛苦劳作。

sensesIntro.en: Grind means to crush into powder, to rub the teeth, or to work long and hard.
sensesIntro.cn: grind 指磨成粉末、磨牙，或长时间辛苦工作。

core.en: Stone pressing grain into dust.
core.cn: 石头把谷物压成粉。

branches.en: A millstone turns slowly.
branches.cn: 磨石缓缓转动。

branches.en: Jaws press together in sleep.
branches.cn: 睡梦中牙关紧咬。

branches.en: A worker repeats the same motion.
branches.cn: 工人重复着同一个动作。

branches.en: Grain and teeth meet the same friction.
branches.cn: 谷物与牙齿，承受同一种摩擦。

branches.en: Endless rubbing wears both stone and person.
branches.cn: 无尽的摩擦，磨石头也磨人。

intro.en: Grind forms irregular verb parts, agents, and compounds.
intro.cn: grind 构成不规则动词形式、施动名词和复合词。

latinIntro.en: Grind has no Latin root; it comes from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: grind 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语。

items.example: He turned the grindstone by hand.

items.exampleCN: 他们重新打磨磨损的刀片。

definition_zh: 澄清；阐明；使（液体）变清
definition_en: to make something easier to understand, or to make a liquid clear by removing the solids in it
core_image: 浑水静置后慢慢变透明
scene: 会议开到一半，投影上的数字互相矛盾。 She asked him to clarify the second point before the vote.
sceneCN: 这里 clarify 指「澄清；阐明」（第 1 个义项：把不清楚的事说明白）；句意是她让他在表决前把第二点讲清楚。

senses.title: To make something understandable
senses.definition: to explain something so that it becomes clear and easy to understand
senses.definitionCN: 加以解释，使某事变得清楚易懂
senses.example: The teacher clarified the rule with one example.
senses.exampleCN: 老师用一个例子把这个规则讲清楚了。
senses.why: The Latin base means bright, so to clarify is literally to make a matter bright.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基本义是明亮的，所以 clarify 字面上就是让事情变亮。

senses.title: To clear a liquid
senses.definition: to make a liquid clear by heating it or removing the solid bits
senses.definitionCN: 通过加热或去除固体微粒使液体变清
senses.example: Melt the butter and clarify it slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 把黄油化开，慢慢澄清。
senses.why: The same brightness image applies to a cloudy liquid that turns transparent.
senses.whyCN: 同样的明亮意象也用于由浑浊变透明的液体。

intro.en: Clarify is built on the Latin adjective for bright, the same root as clarity and clear.
intro.cn: clarify 建立在拉丁语表示明亮的形容词上，与 clarity、clear 同根。

items.en: Clarus meant bright, clear or famous.
items.cn: clarus 意为明亮的、清澈的或闻名的。

items.en: Clarificare meant to make bright or to make plain.
items.cn: clarificare 意为使明亮或使明白。

items.en: Clarifier carried the sense of explaining and of clearing liquid.
items.cn: clarifier 兼有解释与澄清液体的含义。

items.en: English took the verb as clarify in learned and kitchen use.
items.cn: 英语以 clarify 借入，用于学术与厨房两种场合。

items.en: The explaining sense now dominates in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 在日常语言中，解释义如今占主导。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the clarity family, while the meaning group names ways of making things plain.
note.cn: 形近组列出 clarity 家族，近义组列出使事情明白的各种说法。

entries.definition: the quality of being clear and easy to follow
easy to see through or to understand
entries.definitionCN: 容易看透或容易理解的

entries.definition: an explanation that removes doubt
to tell someone how something works
entries.definitionCN: 告诉某人某事如何运作

entries.definition: to make something less complicated
to light something up or make it clear

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the bright root, the cloudy-liquid image and the -ify ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用明亮词根、浑浊液体的意象以及 -ify 后缀。

normal.en: Clarify shares its root with clear and clarity: all three carry brightness.
normal.cn: clarify 与 clear、clarity 同根，三者都带明亮的含义。

normal.en: To clarify is to switch on a lamp in a room where people are guessing.
normal.cn: clarify 就是在大家靠猜的房间里打开一盏灯。

normal.en: The -ify ending means to make, so clarify means to make clear.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ify 表示使成为，所以 clarify 就是使清楚。

normal.en: Butter can be clarified, and so can an argument.
normal.cn: 黄油可以澄清，争论也可以澄清。

normal.en: In meetings, clarify a point is more polite than you are wrong.
normal.cn: 在会上说 clarify a point 比说你错了要客气。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of muddy water settling until the light passes through.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯浑水静置到光线能透过去。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tracing one line on a crowded whiteboard.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在写满字的黑板上划出其中一行。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp switched on above a table of confused faces.
abstract.cn: 想象一张困惑面孔围坐的桌子上方亮起一盏灯。

examples.en: The teacher clarified the rule with one example.
examples.cn: 老师用一个例子把这个规则讲清楚了。

examples.en: Could you clarify what the second figure means?
examples.cn: 你能说明第二个数字是什么意思吗？

examples.en: Melt the butter and clarify it slowly.
examples.cn: 把黄油化开，慢慢澄清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 clar 想成「clear 的兄弟」，ify 想成「使」：使事情清楚，就是澄清。

root: 源自拉丁语 clarus（明亮的、清楚的）与 clarificare（使明亮），经法语 clarifier 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One brightness image serves both a puzzling sentence and a cloudy liquid.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个明亮意象既用于难懂的句子，也用于浑浊的液体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: muddy water settling until it turns transparent.
core.cn: 核心意象：浑水静置，慢慢变得透明。

branches.en: Brightness becomes ease of understanding.
branches.cn: 明亮变成易于理解。

branches.en: The same brightness clears a cloudy liquid.
branches.cn: 同一种明亮感也让浑浊液体变清。

branches.en: Both senses remove whatever blocks the view.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在去除挡住视线的东西。

branches.en: An example works like light on a confusing rule.
branches.cn: 例子就像照在难懂规则上的光。

branches.en: Heat separates the solids and leaves the clear part.
branches.cn: 加热分离出固体，留下清澈的部分。

intro.en: The verb base takes -ify and grows a noun of quality, a noun of action and an instrument noun.
intro.cn: 这个动词词基接 -ify，并长出性质名词、动作名词与工具名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin clarus, bright, which also underlies clear, clarity and declare.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 clarus（明亮的），clear、clarity、declare 也源于它。

items.meaning: the verb with a single subject
items.exampleCN: 她的便条把这个规则讲清楚了。

items.example: He clarified the figures at once.

items.exampleCN: 她正在说明自己的立场。

items.example: The report is praised for its clarity.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告因清晰而受称赞。

items.example: We asked for a short clarification.
items.exampleCN: 我们要求作个简短说明。

items.meaningCN: 使液体变清的设备或药剂
items.example: The tank has a clarifier at the bottom.

items.meaning: forming verbs that mean to make
items.meaningCN: 构成表示使之怎样的动词

latinEntries.example: Clarus is the root of the whole family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: clarus 是整个家族的词根。

definition_zh: 噩梦；梦魇；可怕的处境；令人恐惧的经历
definition_en: a frightening dream, especially one that wakes the sleeper; a very unpleasant or frightening situation or experience
core_image: 深夜床边一团沉重的黑影压在胸口，人想喊却发不出声
scene: 凌晨时分，床边有一团说不清的黑影压下来，人想翻身却动不了，喉咙里发不出声音。 The child woke with a scream after a nightmare about a falling staircase.
sceneCN: 这里是「噩梦」（第 1 个义项：睡眠中令人恐惧的梦）；句意为孩子梦到楼梯塌落，惊叫着醒来。图中可辨识物件：床边黑影、被角、半开的窗。

pos.zh: 噩梦；梦魇；可怕的处境；令人恐惧的经历

collocations.zh: 最可怕的设想；噩梦般的情形
后勤上的噩梦；极难处理的事

derivatives.zh: 由 nightmare 加 -ish（像……的）构成，义为「噩梦般的；可怕的」
由 nightmarish 加 -ly 构成，义为「噩梦般地；可怕地」
由 nightmarish 加 -ness 构成，义为「噩梦般的性质；可怕程度」

senses.title: A frightening dream that wakes the sleeper
senses.titleCN: 噩梦；惊醒人的可怕梦境
senses.definition: a frightening dream, usually so vivid that the sleeper wakes in fear
senses.definitionCN: 令人恐惧的梦，通常逼真到使睡着的人惊醒
senses.example: She woke from a nightmare about falling off a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 她从一个梦见自己从桥上坠落的噩梦中醒来。
senses.why: Old English niht meant night and mare named the demon believed to sit on a sleeper's chest, so the word began as a name for the pressure felt in the dark rather than for the story told afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 niht 是「夜」，mare 指传说中压在睡者胸口的恶魔，所以这个词最初命名的是黑暗中感到的那股压迫，而不是醒来后讲述的情节。

senses.title: The old demon held to sit on a sleeper's chest
senses.titleCN: 梦魇；旧指夜中压身的恶魔
senses.definition: in older use, an evil spirit believed to suffocate people in their sleep, together with the choking sensation it caused
senses.definitionCN: 旧时指被认为在睡眠中使人窒息的恶灵，以及它带来的压迫窒息感
senses.example: In the old tale, a nightmare crouched on the traveller's chest until dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个古老的故事里，一只梦魇蹲在旅人胸口直到天亮。
senses.why: Mare was a demon, not a horse, and the choking weight of sleep paralysis was explained as its body; the modern bad-dream sense grew straight out of that picture.
senses.whyCN: mare 是恶魔而不是母马，睡眠瘫痪时那种被压住的窒息感被解释成它的身体；现代「噩梦」的意思正是从这幅画面长出来的。

senses.title: A situation that feels like a bad dream
senses.titleCN: 可怕的处境；噩梦般的经历
senses.definition: a very unpleasant, difficult or frightening situation or experience
senses.definitionCN: 非常不愉快、艰难或令人恐惧的局面或经历
senses.example: The airport closure turned our trip into a nightmare.
senses.exampleCN: 机场关闭让我们的行程变成了一场噩梦。
senses.why: Once the word names a night terror, calling a day or a journey a nightmare borrows the same helpless fear into waking life, which is why the figurative use needs no new word.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词先命名夜里的恐惧，说某个白天或某趟行程是 nightmare，就是把这股无能为力的恐惧借到清醒生活里，所以比喻义不需要另造新词。

intro.en: Nightmare is a native English compound of night and a word for a demon, and its bad-dream sense is later than the demon it once named.
intro.cn: nightmare 是英语本土的复合词，由「夜」和一个指恶魔的词合成；「噩梦」义比它最初命名的恶魔出现得更晚。

items.en: Niht was the ordinary word for night and supplied the first half of the compound.
items.cn: niht 是古英语里表示「夜」的常用词，构成这个词的前半。

items.en: Mare named an evil spirit or incubus believed to press on sleepers, and it is a different word from mare meaning a female horse.
items.cn: mare 指被认为压住睡者的恶灵或梦淫妖，它与表示母马的 mare 是两个不同的词。

items.en: The compound first named the choking visitation and the terror that came with it, still close to the demon rather than to the dream.
items.cn: 这个复合词最初指夜间压身的侵扰和随之而来的恐惧，仍贴近恶魔本身而不是梦。

items.en: Writers began using nightmare for any frightening dream, and the demon faded into the background of the word; the exact date of this shift is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为，十六至十七世纪的作者开始用 nightmare 指任何可怕的梦，恶魔渐渐退到这个词的背景里；这一转变的确切年代存疑。

items.en: Modern English keeps the dream sense and extends it to any miserable or frightening situation, as in a nightmare journey.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「噩梦」义，并把它扩展到任何糟糕或可怕的情形，如 a nightmare journey。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same night element or sharing the spelling mare; the near-meaning group collects words for bad dreams and the fear they leave behind.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 night 成分构成的词，以及与 mare 拼写相同的词；近义组收表示噩梦和它留下的恐惧的词。

entries.definition: Built from nightmare with -ish, meaning like a nightmare.
entries.definitionCN: 由 nightmare 加 -ish 构成，义为「噩梦般的」。

entries.definition: A female horse, a separate word that merely shares the spelling of the demon in nightmare; the two are unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 母马，只是与 nightmare 里的恶魔同形，两者来源无关。

entries.definition: The time when night begins, built with the same night element.
entries.definitionCN: 夜幕降临的时刻，用了同一个 night 成分。

entries.definition: The hours of darkness, another compound on night.
entries.definitionCN: 黑夜的那段时间，另一个用 night 构成的复合词。

entries.definition: A dream that frightens or disturbs the sleeper, the plain phrase for the dream sense.
entries.definitionCN: 使睡着的人恐惧或不安的梦，是「噩梦」义的普通说法。

entries.definition: Extreme fear, the feeling a nightmare leaves behind.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的恐惧，是噩梦留下的感觉。

entries.definition: A strong feeling of fear and shock, often caused by something seen or imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的恐惧与震惊，常由所见或想象之物引起。

entries.definition: A male demon said to lie upon sleepers, the learned name for the old nightmare creature.
entries.definitionCN: 传说中压住睡者的男性恶魔，是旧时 nightmare 所指之物的书面名称。

normalIntro.en: The word joins the Old English word for night to a demon that was blamed for a weight on the chest, and its later senses keep that picture of helpless fear.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把古英语的「夜」与一个被归咎于胸口重压的恶魔连在一起，后来的义项都保留着那种无力恐惧的画面。

normal.en: Niht is the Old English word for night, so the first half of nightmare is simply the dark hours.
normal.cn: niht 是古英语的「夜」，所以 nightmare 的前半就是那段黑暗的时间。

normal.en: Mare in this word is a demon, not a female horse; the shared spelling is a coincidence of two unrelated words.
normal.cn: 这个词里的 mare 是恶魔，不是母马；拼写相同只是两个无关词偶然撞在一起。

normal.en: The demon was blamed for the choking weight felt during sleep paralysis, which is why the word first meant that oppression.
normal.cn: 睡眠瘫痪时感到的压身窒息被归咎于这个恶魔，所以这个词最初指的就是那股压迫。

normal.en: The dream sense came later, when the demon was forgotten and only the terror of the dream remained.
normal.cn: 「梦」这个意思来得更晚：恶魔被遗忘之后，只剩梦里的恐惧留在词里。

normal.en: The figurative sense grows straight out of the dream: a nightmare journey is a waking experience that feels equally out of control.
normal.cn: 比喻义直接从梦里长出来：a nightmare journey 就是一段同样失控的清醒经历。

abstract.en: A word invented to explain a weight on the chest ends up naming a broken schedule, because both feel like something sitting on you that you cannot push off.
abstract.cn: 一个原本用来解释胸口重压的词，最后用来命名被打乱的日程，因为两者都像有东西压在身上、推不开。

abstract.en: Nightmare keeps two unrelated words in one shell, the demon and the horse, and only the demon shaped the meaning.
abstract.cn: nightmare 把一个恶魔和一个母马两个无关的词装进同一个外壳，真正塑造词义的只有那个恶魔。

abstract.en: Every figurative nightmare is a claim that the daytime world has started behaving like a bad dream, with no exit until you wake.
abstract.cn: 每一个比喻意义上的 nightmare，都是在说白天的世界开始像噩梦一样运转，不醒来就找不到出口。

examples.en: She woke from a nightmare about falling off a bridge.
examples.cn: 她从一个梦见自己从桥上坠落的噩梦中醒来。

examples.en: The flooding turned the rescue into a nightmare for the whole team.
examples.cn: 洪水让整个救援队陷入噩梦般的困境。

examples.en: He still has nightmares about the accident.
examples.cn: 他仍会梦到那场事故。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奈特妹儿」——夜里有个黑影压在身上，想喊也喊不出声；nightmare 就是噩梦。

root: 古英语 niht（夜）加 mare（传说中压住睡者的恶灵，一般认为与表示母马的 mare 无关）；词义由「夜间压身的恐惧」扩展为噩梦与可怕处境。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a night terror caused by a weight on the chest; the senses then divide into the bad dream, the old demon, and the waking situation that feels the same.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是夜里胸口受压带来的恐惧；义项由此分出噩梦、旧时的恶魔，以及感觉相同的清醒处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy dark shape at the bedside pressing on the chest while the sleeper cannot speak.
core.cn: 核心意象：床边一团沉重的黑影压住胸口，睡着的人说不出话。

branches.en: a child sitting up in the dark, calling for a parent
branches.cn: 孩子在黑暗里坐起来喊父母

branches.en: an old woodcut of a demon crouched on a sleeper's chest
branches.cn: 一幅旧木刻里蹲在睡者胸口的恶魔

branches.en: the same choking weight described first as a spirit, then as a dream
branches.cn: 同一种压身的窒息感，先说成恶灵，后说成梦

branches.en: a cancelled flight turning a holiday into a nightmare
branches.cn: 航班取消，把假期变成噩梦

branches.en: a schedule so tight that every delay spreads
branches.cn: 紧到任何延误都会扩散的日程

intro.en: The word is held together by the Old English noun for night, the demon word mare, the compound they formed and the English endings that build its adjective and adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的「夜」、指恶魔的 mare、二者合成的复合词，以及构成形容词和副词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The mare in nightmare is a demon of Germanic folklore, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: nightmare 里的 mare 是日耳曼民间传说中的恶魔，没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 前任；前（前缀）；例（缩写）
definition_en: a former partner, or a prefix meaning former
core_image: 旧相册里被剪掉一半的合影
scene: 谈到过去的婚姻时，他只说了一句「她是我的前任」。 When talking about his past marriage, he only said that she was his ex.
sceneCN: 这里 ex 是「前任」（第 1 个义项：过去的伴侣）；句意：谈到过去的婚姻时，他只说了一句「她是我的前任」。

senses.title: Former partner
senses.definition: a former husband, wife, or partner
senses.definitionCN: 以前的丈夫、妻子或伴侣
senses.example: He is still friends with his ex.
senses.exampleCN: 他和前任仍然是朋友。
senses.why: The prefix ex- means out or former, and stands alone in speech.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 ex- 意为出或以前，在口语中可单独使用。

senses.title: Former
senses.definition: a prefix meaning former
senses.definitionCN: 表示「以前的」的前缀
senses.example: Her ex-husband lives abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她的前夫住在国外。
senses.why: The prefix attaches to titles and relations.
senses.whyCN: 这个前缀附着在称谓和关系词前。

senses.title: Example abbreviation
senses.definition: a written short form of example
senses.definitionCN: example 的书面缩写
senses.example: See ex. 3 on the next page.
senses.exampleCN: 见下一页的例 3。
senses.why: Dictionaries shorten example to ex. in cross-references.
senses.whyCN: 词典在交叉引用中把 example 缩写成 ex.。

intro.en: Ex comes from the Latin preposition ex, meaning out of.
intro.cn: ex 来自拉丁语介词 ex（出自、向外）。

items.en: Ex means out of.
items.cn: ex 意为出自、向外。

items.en: The prefix ex- marks former status.
items.cn: 前缀 ex- 标记以前的身份。

items.en: Ex- appears in ex-wife and ex-king.
items.cn: ex- 出现在 ex-wife 与 ex-king 中。

items.en: Ex stands alone as a noun for a former partner.
items.cn: ex 可单独作名词，指前任。

items.en: The abbreviation ex. also shortens example.
items.cn: 缩写 ex. 也用来缩短 example。

note.en: Ex as a noun names a former partner; the prefix ex- marks former status.
note.cn: ex 作名词指前任；前缀 ex- 标记以前的身份。

entries.definition: former
a former wife
more than one former partner
belonging to an earlier time
coming before the present one
a person one is close to

normalIntro.en: Ex is the small word for someone now outside your life.
normalIntro.cn: ex 是那个现在已经不在你生活里的人的小词。

normal.en: His ex means his former partner.
normal.cn: his ex 意为他的前任。

normal.en: Ex-wife means a former wife.
normal.cn: ex-wife 意为前妻。

normal.en: Ex-husband means a former husband.
normal.cn: ex-husband 意为前夫。

normal.en: Ex-boyfriend means a former boyfriend.
normal.cn: ex-boyfriend 意为前男友。

normal.en: Compare former: ex- is a prefix, former is a full adjective.
normal.cn: 对比 former：ex- 是前缀，former 是完整形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a photo cut in half, leaving one person.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被剪掉一半、只剩一人的合影。

abstract.en: Imagine a door marked out, with the room still full of light.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇标着「出」的门，房间里仍有光。

abstract.en: Think of a name with a small line drawn through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被画了一道小线的名字。

examples.en: She met her ex at a friend's wedding.
examples.cn: 她在朋友的婚礼上遇到了前任。

examples.en: He works with his ex-wife.
examples.cn: 他和前妻一起工作。

examples.en: My ex-boyfriend moved to another city.
examples.cn: 我的前男友搬到了另一座城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex」只有两个字母——像一个被划掉的名字前面的小叉，表示「以前的」。

root: 拉丁语 ex（出）→ 前缀 ex-（以前的）→ 口语名词 ex（前任）。

sensesIntro.en: Ex begins as a Latin word for out, becomes a prefix for former, and then stands alone to name a former partner.
sensesIntro.cn: ex 从拉丁语「出」开始，成为表示「以前的」前缀，最后单独指前任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a photo cut in half, leaving one person.
core.cn: 核心意象：被剪掉一半、只剩一人的合影。

branches.en: A former partner is the spoken noun.
branches.cn: 前任是口语中的名词用法。

branches.en: The prefix marks former status.
branches.cn: 前缀标记以前的身份。

branches.en: The abbreviation shortens example.
branches.cn: 缩写形式缩短 example。

branches.en: The noun grew out of the prefix.
branches.cn: 名词由前缀发展而来。

branches.en: Prefix and abbreviation both save space.
branches.cn: 前缀与缩写都在节省空间。

intro.en: Ex is both a Latin prefix and a small English word.
intro.cn: ex 既是拉丁前缀，也是一个简短的英语单词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex, out of, is the source of the prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ex（出自）是前缀的来源。

items.exampleCN: ex 在口语中单独使用。

items.example: Ex-wife joins the prefix to wife.
items.exampleCN: ex-wife 把前缀与 wife 结合。
ex. 在印刷中缩短 example。

latinEntries.example: Ex is the source of the prefix.

definition_zh: 协调；配合；协调能力；并列关系
definition_en: the act of making parts work together, the ability to move smoothly, or a balanced link in grammar
core_image: 几根线在同一只手里被收拢，拧成一股结实的绳
scene: 救援现场最缺的不是人手，而是让各队同时行动的那份安排。 Good coordination kept the teams from getting in each other's way.
sceneCN: 这里 coordination 指「协调；配合」（第 1 个义项：让不同部分协同运作）；句意是良好的协调让各队没有互相妨碍。

senses.title: The working of parts together
senses.definition: the act of organizing people or parts so that they work well together
senses.definitionCN: 把人员或部分组织起来使其配合良好的行为
senses.example: The rescue depended on close coordination.
senses.exampleCN: 这次救援依靠紧密的协调。
senses.why: Many hands move faster only when they move on one plan.
senses.whyCN: 许多双手只有在同一份计划上才动得更快。

senses.title: Smooth control of the body
senses.definition: the ability to move different parts of the body smoothly together
senses.definitionCN: 让身体各部分顺畅配合的能力
senses.example: Dancing improved her coordination.
senses.exampleCN: 跳舞改善了她的协调能力。
senses.why: The body is also a team, and it too needs a manager.
senses.whyCN: 身体也是一支队伍，也需要一个调度者。

senses.title: A balanced grammatical link
senses.definition: a grammatical connection between two parts of equal rank
senses.definitionCN: 两个同级部分之间的语法连接
senses.example: The sentence uses coordination, not subordination.
senses.exampleCN: 这个句子用的是并列关系，不是从属关系。
senses.why: Grammar also likes things to stand level, hand in hand.
senses.whyCN: 语法也喜欢让事物平起平坐、手拉着手。

intro.en: Coordination comes from Latin coordinatio, from coordinare, to arrange together, built from co-, together, and ordo, order.
intro.cn: coordination 来自拉丁语 coordinatio，源于 coordinare（一同排列），由 co-（一起）与 ordo（次序）构成。

items.en: Ordo meant a row, a rank or a fixed arrangement.
items.cn: ordo 意为行列、等级或固定的排列。

items.en: Coordinare meant to set several things into one arrangement.
items.cn: coordinare 意为把几样事物排进同一个安排。

items.en: Coordinatio named the state of being arranged together.
items.cn: coordinatio 指被一同排列的状态。

items.en: English coordination first described equal rank in logic.
items.cn: 英语 coordination 最初描述逻辑中的同级关系。

items.en: It now covers teamwork, muscles and grammar alike.
items.cn: 今天它同时涵盖团队协作、肌肉动作与语法关系。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin ordering base ordin-, and the meaning group names other forms of joint effort.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的排列词基 ordin-，近义组列出其他表示共同出力的说法。

entries.definition: to make parts work together
a person who organizes joint work
the act of making someone a priest
the act of working with others
the arranging of things into a working whole
entries.definitionCN: 把事物安排成运作的整体

entries.definition: joint effort by a group

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with threads gathered into one hand, then move to a body moving as one and to clauses side by side.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从几根线被收进一只手开始，再到身体像一个整体那样动，最后到并排的分句。

normal.en: Coordination is the noun behind coordinate: the result of setting things in one order.
normal.cn: coordination 是 coordinate 背后的名词：把事物排进同一顺序之后的成果。

normal.en: Think of a rowing crew: eight oars, one rhythm.
normal.cn: 想象一支赛艇队：八支桨，一个节奏。

normal.en: Hand-eye coordination is the same idea inside one body.
normal.cn: 手眼协调就是同一个道理，只是装在一个身体里。

normal.en: In grammar, coordination joins equals; subordination joins unequals.
normal.cn: 语法里，并列连接平等者，从属连接不平等者。

normal.en: The longer word carries the calmer, more official tone.
normal.cn: 这个词更长，语气也更沉稳、更正式。

abstract.en: Picture several threads closing into one knot.
abstract.cn: 想象几根线收拢成一个结。

abstract.en: Picture eight rowers pulling at the same instant.
abstract.cn: 想象八名桨手在同一瞬间发力。

abstract.en: Picture two dancers turning without a word.
abstract.cn: 想象两名舞者不说一句话就转身同步。

examples.en: The festival ran smoothly thanks to careful coordination.
examples.cn: 多亏细致的协调，节庆活动顺利进行。

examples.en: Her coordination improved after months of practice.
examples.cn: 练习几个月后，她的协调能力提高了。

examples.en: The plan was made in coordination with local schools.
examples.cn: 这项计划是与当地学校协同制定的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 coordination 记成 co（一起）加 ordin（次序）加 ation：让各方进入同一个次序，就是协调。

root: 源自拉丁语 coordinare（一同排列）的名词 coordinatio，由 co-（一起）与 ordo（次序）构成，后引申为身体协调与语法并列。

sensesIntro.en: From many threads held in one hand, to a body moving as one, and at last to two clauses standing level.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一只手拢住的许多线，到像一个整体那样动的身体，最后到并排而立的分句。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several threads twisted into one strong cord.
core.cn: 核心意象：几根线被拧成一股结实的绳。

branches.en: Separate groups agree on one plan and one time.
branches.cn: 分开的群体就同一份计划与时间达成一致。

branches.en: Muscles and eyes learn to work as a single unit.
branches.cn: 肌肉与眼睛学会作为一个整体运作。

branches.en: Two equal parts are joined without either ruling.
branches.cn: 两个平等的部分相连，谁都不统治谁。

branches.en: Both senses are about smooth joint movement.
branches.cn: 两个义项都关乎顺畅的共同动作。

branches.en: A body and a sentence both need balanced parts.
branches.cn: 身体与句子都需要彼此平衡的部分。

intro.en: Coordination is coordinate plus -ion, resting on Latin co-, together, and ordo, order.
intro.cn: coordination 是 coordinate 加 -ion，根源是拉丁语 co-（一起）与 ordo（次序）。

latinIntro.en: The ordering base ordin- also appears in order, ordinary and subordinate.
latinIntro.cn: 排列词基 ordin- 也出现在 order、ordinary 与 subordinate 中。

items.meaning: the joining of parts in one order
items.meaningCN: 把各部分排进同一顺序

items.exampleCN: 从属分句要依附别的分句。
